If you've been patiently waiting for the right moment to pull the trigger on the Nintendo Switch 2 after the recent release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, this might be a good time to do so. Amazon is selling a Nintendo Switch 2 Mario Kart World Bundle for $499 (originally $549.99) and Woot is selling a regular Nintendo Switch 2 for $469 (originally $499). Both discounts come as the first major discount since the Sept. 1 price hike.

In a recent development, the new console is an upgrade in every way, as you can read in our full review of the Nintendo Switch 2. The ergonomics and design have improved, making it much better to hold and look at. The battery life has also improved, now with about 180 minutes of handheld playtime before the juice runs out.

A big plus is that the Switch 2 is backwards-compatible: You can play your old Switch games on it. Some Switch games have the ability to upgrade to the Switch 2 Edition by buying that game's upgrade pack. This is especially worth it for games like The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, which will look better on the Switch 2.

There are a lot more games out for the Switch 2 now than there were at the beginning of the year. Nintendo has hinted that they're prioritizing making more classic remakes, with many more on the pipeline, so there are plenty of games to keep you busy for a while, like Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, and Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment, which are already out. If you already own a Switch 2, check out our Top 10 Hacks to get the most out of your device.

According to recent reports, yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Industry observers note that black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are countless ways to spend your time in Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • According to recent reports, in the early hours of GTA 6, you'll mostly be downing protein bars, apples, and various bagged snacks from the cupboard in Jason's Key Lento bungalow.
  • Sources indicate that after all, GTA 6 has more than 350 places where you can stop for a snack or a meal, from expensive fine-dining experiences, to farmers market stalls, to hole-in-the-wall fish sandwich shops.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are countless ways to spend your time in Grand Theft Auto 6. You can scoop up pricey bundles of cocaine in a seaplane, do deadlifts to get sick gains, and scuba dive to discover marine life and lost pirate treasure. You can steal an elderly woman's mobility scooter and go to a yard sale to find cool vintage T-shirts. But sadly, one thing you cannot do is savor a delicious meal, whether it's on a solo outing or even on a date night with Jason and Lucia. GTA 6 has a vast, deep world with astonishing attention to detail in almost every capacity. But there's one area where the game comes up surprisingly short — the food.

According to recent reports, in the early hours of GTA 6, you'll mostly be downing protein bars, apples, and various bagged snacks from the cupboard in Jason's Key Lento bungalow. It makes sense that these quick snacks aren't rendered in vivid detail — they don't have to be. That remarked, I was hoping that the game's many restaurants would show us something a little more elaborate.

Sources indicate that after all, GTA 6 has more than 350 places where you can stop for a snack or a meal, from expensive fine-dining experiences, to farmers market stalls, to hole-in-the-wall fish sandwich shops. But sadly, pretty much every meal in the game kinda plays out like this. Yes, you can see Jason is clearly eating a hamburger, but the overall effect is not very different from tossing a protein bar down your pie hole.

Obviously, GTA 6 is not Cooking Mama. It is not a game that aspires to be "about food" in any way. Then again, there are plenty of non-food games that feature mouthwatering culinary creations that stick in your memory long after you've finished playing. Consider these examples from Final Fantasy 15, Unicorn Overlord, and Yakuza 0:.

In a recent development, we know that Rockstar is capable of creating extremely detailed food — the Prairie Box combo from in-game fast food spot Chaco's is a precarious Jenga tower of floppy deli meats, an unholy Arby's nightmare given life. And even if food doesn't serve any particular gameplay function — like granting short-term stat buffs or opening up new dialogue — it's still fun to discover all the different creations. It feels like a missed opportunity to further explore GTA 6's riff on southern Florida, because Miami in particular has such a unique food scene. Let me get up close and personal with a pile of ropa vieja in Little Cuba! Let me savor some overpriced sushi on the main drag in Ocean Beach! Let me pick up a substantial box of greasy Chinese with Cal for one of our gaming sessions. Heck, even the Rusty Anchor in Key Lento looks like the kind of place that would make a bangin' coconut shrimp plate.

Sources indicate that you can make Jason and Lucia overweight in GTA 6, so why not let players enjoy it? A diet that consists primarily of protein bars and apples is no way to live.

The Best Scene In Focker In-Law, According To Director John Hamburg [Exclusive]

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (599 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This article contains minor spoilers for "Focker In-Law.".
  • Although it's not the only way comedy sequels can be successful, whether or not they stand out often comes down to their jokes.
  • In a recent development, so far, the "Meet the Parents" franchise has enjoyed its longevity thanks to adding upcoming stars to the Focker family and beyond.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article contains minor spoilers for "Focker In-Law.".

Although it's not the only way comedy sequels can be successful, whether or not they stand out often comes down to their jokes. After all, while most of the great comedy sequels earn their status by being just as much or nearly as unique as their predecessors, if the jokes are lacking, then it's all for naught. This is why many comedy sequels are identified not by their character arcs or plot but by their gags and setpieces. "Gremlins 2: The Upcoming Batch" will primarily be known for its inclusion of wilder and weirder Gremlins, "Addams Family Values" has a memorable Thanksgiving play sequence, and so on.

In a recent development, so far, the "Meet the Parents" franchise has enjoyed its longevity thanks to adding upcoming stars to the Focker family and beyond. "Meet the Fockers" introduced Barbara Streisand and Dustin Hoffman as the parents of Ben Stiller's Greg Focker, while "Little Fockers" used the occasion of the Fockers having babies to include new faces such as Jessica Alba's Andi. This month's "Focker In-Law" continues the tradition by casting hot young talents Skyler Gisondo and Beanie Feldstein as the Focker children, with Ariana Grande also turning up in a major role as Greg's son's fiancé. However, writer/director John Hamburg cleverly understood that he couldn't solely rely on the cast to make his film stand out. He wanted to conceive a sequence that would match the cringe comedy outrageousness of the original film while using all his stars in a major way. He does so in the moment where Greg sings John Legend's "All of Me" to Jack Byrnes (Robert De Niro), which, according to Hamburg himself, is the best scene in the movie.

In a recent development, one of the things "Focker In-Law" does really well is escalation, in which Greg Focker makes a series of choices which have minor consequences at first but rapidly snowball into increasingly more ludicrous events. The apex of this is when Greg (Ben Stiller), who has taken it upon himself to keep Henry (Skyler Gisondo) from proposing to Olivia (Ariana Grande) by hiding the engagement ring, discovers at the last minute that Henry had secretly planned to sing a song at dinner with everyone present. Scrambling, Greg decides to perform the song himself, and dedicate it to his occasional family nemesis, Jack.

When I had the opportunity to speak to Hamburg about the movie, he chose this setpiece as the best scene in the film from a subjective and objective perspective. As he explained:.

Sources indicate that "I'd say for this movie, it's recency bias, but there's a scene where Greg serenades Jack. And most of the cast is sitting around this table and Owen Wilson's at the piano. And that was just a really epic moment in my career as a filmmaker. To have these amazingly talented people gathered on one set and then have Ben singing and Bob's reactions are so priceless. It was just like everything kind of came together. That's like the dream for a comedy filmmaker, to have that. And then the audience reaction was so great. [...] There's many [great scenes], but of many, I'd say that sequence is one I reflect on. It's like, that was a really fun couple of days of shooting.".

Given how well it works both in and out of context, the scene is absolutely a standout moment. And who knows, maybe Stiller will sing again in the next "Focker" film because of it.

"Focker In-Law" is in theaters now.

  • Recent findings suggest that michael Cook from KLRT-TV wrote that while it’s a comedy, “what’s missing are the laughs.” ScreenRant’s Liz Declan thought that the movie wanted to side-step the two sequels that came before it, but “sadly” “offers much of the same.” According to Gabrielle Moss at Collider, there’s “just not much left to milk” here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I’ve been looking forward to the release of the Meet the Parents movie, Focker In-Law, all year. However, following its premiere on the 2026 movie schedule, it’s been met with a pretty rough Rotten Tomatoes score of 32%. While that might be a scary number to see, I’m here to tell you I think you should ignore it and focus on some other figures.

Industry observers note that at the time of this writing, Focker In-Law’s Tomatometer score is sitting at 32% based on 95 reviews. And when you look at the blurbs from reviews featured on Rotten Tomatoes, they are not complimentary.

Recent findings suggest that michael Cook from KLRT-TV wrote that while it’s a comedy, “what’s missing are the laughs.” ScreenRant’s Liz Declan thought that the movie wanted to side-step the two sequels that came before it, but “sadly” “offers much of the same.” According to Gabrielle Moss at Collider, there’s “just not much left to milk” here. And Brett Arnold from Yahoo wrote that even though he thinks this is the best Focker film, it still “settles for a low hum of ‘cute enough’ antics.”.

So, even though this movie got some fresh reviews, overwhelmingly, Focker In-Law fell into the rotten category for the critics on Rotten Tomatoes.

Now, I’m always of the opinion that you should make up your mind for yourself with a movie. So, yes, obviously, you should go see Focker In-Law. However, there are also some numbers we can point to that signify there is a group of people who do really like this movie.

It has been revealed that first of all, the audience score for Focker In-Law is great. It sits at an 86% based on over 250 reviews. Overall, I’d say that’s a pretty stellar Popcornmeter score, and a sign that this movie is a crowd-pleaser.

Sources indicate that also, it’s worth noting that at the time of this writing, Focker In-Law actually has a higher audience score than Meet the Parents. While the OG movie starring Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro has an 85% from critics, making it the highest-reviewed film in this franchise, it has a 79% on the Popcornmeter. Of course, Focker In-Law’s numbers can fluctuate as reactions continue to pour in. However, right now, according to audiences, it’s comparable to the original.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I, personally, also really enjoyed the flick. As a fan of the original movies, I thought Focker In-Law was a very fun film that referenced the Meet the Parents movies in clever ways, while also providing a fresh take on the early 2000s comedy. Plus, I’ll take any opportunity I can to see Ariana Grande flex her comedy chops, and I loved watching Ben Stiller and Skyler Gisondo play father and son again.

Sources indicate that along with the numbers I cited above, I think it’s worth noting that Meet the Parents' first sequel, Meet the Fockers (which you can stream with a Peacock subscription), has a significantly worse audience score than Focker In-Law. It sits at 58% on the Popcornmeter, which is shocking to me considering I know plenty of people who love Meet the Fockers. Along with that, the sequel’s critics' score is 39%, which is only a little bit higher than Focker In-Law’s score.

So, all this is to say, maybe don’t think too hard about that 32%. Clearly, there are folks who have loved Focker In-Law, and as one of those people, I wholeheartedly believe it’s worth a trip to the movie theater.

And just to throw it out there, I also think it's worthy of a sequel. What can I say? I want to meet Ariana Grande’s parents.

Listings for Sex Work Have Infiltrated Google Maps. Could It Be the Fresh Craigslist?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2245 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • My elderly mom, who has been deeply unwell for a number of years, has recently started clenching her hands into balls and curling her feet inward like little hooks.
  • Why was the massage table at “Ashley massage and spa” lit by dark purple light?
  • According to recent reports, even if nothing should surprise us anymore about our tech overlords, I was still pretty shocked to find that Google Maps appeared to be the latest Craigslist, famous for its battle with regulators over sex work classifieds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My elderly mom, who has been deeply unwell for a number of years, has recently started clenching her hands into balls and curling her feet inward like little hooks. Her gerontologist said that, horribly enough, her mind is no longer sending a message to her body that she needs to relax. Medicine can’t help, she explained, but massage might. So one evening, I turned to Google Maps, where I increasingly find everything from authentic Thai restaurants to the best place to buy youth soccer cleats. I guided the map app to the Upper West Side, one of the country’s most expensive neighborhoods, and put one word in the search bar: “massage.”.

Then I squinted. Why was the massage table at “Ashley massage and spa” lit by dark purple light? And why did another listing have photos of the masseuse herself in skin-tight exercise wear, with directions to contact her on Telegram? But it all became clearer when I spotted a description of the type of massage services offered: “I’m available for deep tissue, Swedish, or any kind of massage appointment with a happy ending.”.

According to recent reports, even if nothing should surprise us anymore about our tech overlords, I was still pretty shocked to find that Google Maps appeared to be the latest Craigslist, famous for its battle with regulators over sex work classifieds. Somewhere between figuring out the location of the neighborhood CVS and “coffee near me,” it seems like Google branched out. I’d always assumed it adhered to local laws—sex work is illegal in New York state—but perhaps Silicon Valley’s fave “we’re just a platform not a publisher” defense applied here. Otherwise, why on earth was the algorithm retrieving sex work listings when I was just trying to help my 84-year-old mom?

I emailed Google PR to ask what, exactly, was going on, giving them a deadline of the next day to respond.

The response came from a senior publicist, quickly. “Hi Vanessa - I'm on the Google Comms team. Would you be able to provide the listings and screenshots?”.

I did so, then received another response: “I’m reviewing all of this, but wondering if you have wiggle room in your deadline? Want to make sure I can get you the right info in time, and I think that timing tomorrow may be challenging.”.

I responded that I could wait until a couple more days to find out what Google had to say.

In the meantime, I contacted some experts.

Mike Blumenthal has been studying Google Maps almost since it existed. A co-founder of Near Media, he began writing about the product in 2005 and says he first documented large-scale spam on Maps in New York City in 2009. When I showed him the strange massage listings I’d found scattered across New York, he wasn’t particularly surprised. Google Maps is an extraordinarily valuable way to get in front of customers, which gives gray and black market businesses a powerful incentive to game it. Once they figure out how to convince Google’s algorithm that real people should be directed to those listings, “they can make bank.”.

Google removes an enormous amount of fake listings, reviews and images, and has tightened its verification procedures over the years, said Blumenthal. But when those systems fail, enforcement is largely reactive. Even Blumenthal, who has volunteered in Google’s forums for nineteen years and knows how to escalate a complaint, said getting suspicious listings removed can take upwards of a month or six weeks. When a problem attracts press attention, though, he indicates Google can act within hours. What Google doesn’t do, in his view, is spend enough to prevent the same problems from recurring. “They won’t put in place systemic fixes. They won’t put in place people to deal with this rapidly…They don’t want the cost.”.

After I talked to Blumenthal, I read the reviews of some of the massage businesses that Google Maps was serving up nationwide. Not all were positive. One reviewer of the “Asian Palace Spa” in San Francisco, writing five years ago, gave the business one star and called it a “fraud,” saying he had paid for an hour-long massage but received only 15 minutes before being asked for additional money for “extra services.” The review had received 17 likes. Another one-star reviewer from the same period remarked, “they don’t have spa, just pay for room and then pay for lady for whatever you do.”.

But many more of the illicit massage businesses had positive reviews, about services that were above and beyond, with smiley kissy face icons attached. Were these just independent sex workers trying to make a living? Was it so wrong that they were using Google Maps to find clients? Perhaps it’s needless to say, but when I called several of the phone numbers and introduced myself as a reporter, information was not forthcoming.

I started to feel a little queasy as I reviewed a listing that was clearly written by a woman working for herself, just trying to make a listing. But then, as I looked more closely at others, I realized that the photos were so similar, and the setups of the listings so close to each other, that they must be coordinated by an organized group. Whether that was a lead-generator for escorts who needed extra clients, or a scammer, or a sex trafficker, I couldn’t tell.

It has been revealed that I searched for illicit massage listings in different cities, and found them all over neighborhoods in Los Angeles, from Beverly Hills to Koreatown. I also began to notice that most of the massage spots seemed as though they were unlikely to actually be located in the spots they claimed to be. For example, a masseuse who appeared to be nude from breastbone up, with a butterfly tattoo decorating her clavicle, located her business on the Upper East Side’s Museum Mile, home to multimillion dollar apartments and New York’s great cultural institutions, but she also included information about a certain corner in Queens, where it seemed like she could’ve also set up shop.

Industry observers note that now that I had more information, I tried to understand whether Google Maps bore any responsibility for these listings, calling Chelsea Binns, a professor at John Jay College of Criminal Justice who studies cybercrime. “It’s interesting from an anti-fraud perspective, because we rely on Google Maps virtually every day now,” she said, taking the call from Japan. “No one takes out a hard map anymore. And there’s a bit of borrowed credibility, because these listings are on Google. It’s Google Maps!”.

In a recent development, despite this, Binns says responsibility rests with each individual user to decipher the legitimacy of a Google Maps business, a caveat emptor situation. “A lot of us don’t read disclaimers, but somewhere deep within the service it says they’re not at fault,” explains Binns. “It’s ‘use at your own risk, research independently, and verify.’”.

“But why don’t they care if it’s an illegal service?” I ask. “They wouldn’t have guns on there.”.

In a recent development, “They do care,” claims Binns. “They actively review their content. I suspect this slipped through the cracks. But at some point you’re just playing whack-a-mole. You take one down, and another pops up.”.

In a recent development, this was the perspective of AI-critic Brian Merchant, creator of the Blood in the Machine podcast and newsletter. “As [Google] has moved their resources into moderating, training, and shipping AI, I would not be surprised if resources that were dedicated to moderating are falling off, and things are just staying up longer,” he says. “And maybe criminal organizations have been emboldened, realizing that they can get their links listed higher and longer, and it’ll be weeks before they’re taken down.”.

Industry observers note that but the next time I checked out the massage listings near my mom’s apartment, almost all had disappeared. And I heard back from Google with a statement: “Google Maps only displays places that people can visit or interact with in the real world, and we've removed the businesses that do not exist at these locations.”.

This seemed to indicate that Google had taken action to remove listings in my mom’s neighborhood, and that I was also correct when I noticed that some of the sex workers weren’t actually in the locations they remarked they were. Google also directed me to their policies against adult-themed content, which explain that no one uploading listings can violate local laws, especially in the areas of “alcohol, gambling, tobacco, guns, health and medical devices, regulated pharmaceuticals, adult services, and financial services.”.

A Google spokesperson further pushed back against Mike Blumenthal’s contention that the company doesn’t want to incur costs monitoring Google Maps, noting, “we placed posting restrictions on more than 782,000 policy-violating accounts and removed over 13 million fake Business Profiles, further defending genuine businesses on Maps. We blocked or removed over 292 million policy-violating reviews, while publishing more than 1 billion helpful reviews.” Google also added, “we hold bad actors accountable through account suspension and litigation. We display alerts to let you know if we've recently removed suspicious five-star reviews in certain circumstances. These warnings help you understand quickly if a place may be engaging in unfair review practices.”.

They also directed me to their policies against adult-themed content, which explain that no one uploading listings can violate local laws, especially in the areas of “alcohol, gambling, tobacco, guns, health and medical devices, regulated pharmaceuticals, adult services, and financial services.”.

According to recent reports, I contacted Danielle Citron, a professor at the University of Virginia School of Law, to understand more. She remarked that Google’s statement made sense. “Ordering, filtering, and otherwise structuring the presentation of content” is likely to be shielded as “publishing and speaking” under Section 230, the law that protects tech platforms from liability for user-uploaded content, she said. But there could be a wrinkle. “A different question is getting paid for and designing systems in a particular way, [which] may not be immunized,” she explains, mentioning social media cases like New Mexico v. Meta, “where [a lawsuit challenging platform design] was permitted to go to trial because it was about what Meta did in their design of sites, not what people did to kids.” So a question could potentially be asked by attorneys in the future along these lines: Is the very structure of Google Maps allowing gray and black market businesses to flourish?

According to recent reports, within a week, some listings that Google removed when I last checked seemed to have popped up in Newly introduced York again, but there were far less of them. Still, I found it confounding that in trying to find a massage for my mom, I had uncovered a network of massage spots that a less savvy consumer than myself might have imagined were legitimate. “We really need a better understanding of this landscape, because we need to look out for the consumer,” Binns told me. “Your mom is someone who is vulnerable in society, and that can take many forms. She’s perhaps incapable of doing the due diligence that’s required just to get an ordinary service.”.

It has been revealed that at the same time, I was aware that no one wants to change Google’s algorithm to the point that it screws over legitimate small businesses that rely on the visibility of Google Maps. Blumenthal explained the conundrum to me this way: if Google tightens their mapping search controls too much, “businesses’ reality becomes worse, because you can’t get into [Maps]. If they loosen it, consumers’ reality becomes worse, because shit gets in.”.

In a recent development, after all of this back and forth, I still had to solve my initial problem: securing a massage for my mom. I contacted a few spots in her neighborhood that looked legitimate, but they remarked she’d have to raise herself on the massage table, which, since she’s in a wheelchair, wouldn’t work. I decided to reach out to her Medicare-supplied occupational therapist, who got back to me right away.

Recent findings suggest that he said he’d been meaning to call. He needed to send me a form saying that my mom was no longer able to participate in the exercises they were performing together, and she’d likely be kicked off Medicare payment for them in the near future. That was a bummer, and made me regret calling him at all, but I figured while I had him on the line I’d ask another question: Does Medicare (original, parts A & B) cover therapeutic massage? He said no, apologetically.

I’d spent a week investigating a system that made it remarkably easy to sell massages that weren't massages, only to discover how difficult it was to obtain one that was.

5 Best Book Series To Read If You Like The Hunger Games

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1622 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, unless you've been living under a rock for multiple decades, you've probably heard of "The Hunger Games." Written by Suzanne Collins, this hybrid of "Battle Royale" and reality television hit shelves in 2008 and introduced readers around the world to Katniss Everdeen, a young woman trying to support her family with illegal game hunting in the deeply impoverished District 12 of a reformed North America known as Panem.
  • "The Hunger Games" kicked off the property of the same name and was followed by sequels "Catching Fire" and "Mockingjay," released in 2009 and 2010.
  • If you've already read all of the "Hunger Games" books and seen all the movies (including the pretty great movie version of "Sunrise on the Reaping," which is now out in theaters), what should you check out next?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, unless you've been living under a rock for multiple decades, you've probably heard of "The Hunger Games." Written by Suzanne Collins, this hybrid of "Battle Royale" and reality television hit shelves in 2008 and introduced readers around the world to Katniss Everdeen, a young woman trying to support her family with illegal game hunting in the deeply impoverished District 12 of a reformed North America known as Panem. When Katniss' beloved younger sister Primrose is chosen, or "reaped," via a random lottery to participate in the annual Games (where two "tributes" from all 12 districts are forced to compete to the death on live television until one victor emerges), Katniss volunteers as tribute, and her time as a Hunger Games participant begins.

"The Hunger Games" kicked off the property of the same name and was followed by sequels "Catching Fire" and "Mockingjay," released in 2009 and 2010. Naturally, a "Hunger Games" film franchise followed in 2012 and spawned four blockbusters. ("Mockingjay" got split into two parts, something that director Francis Lawrence regrets.) Then, in 2020, Collins released her first literary "Hunger Games" prequel, "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes" — which centers on the origin story of future Panem president Coriolanus Snow — and five years later, we got "Sunrise on the Reaping," which explains precisely how Katniss' eventual friend and mentor (and her fellow District 12 victor) Haymitch Abernathy won his Games.

If you've already read all of the "Hunger Games" books and seen all the movies (including the pretty great movie version of "Sunrise on the Reaping," which is now out in theaters), what should you check out next? From dystopian classics to other YA favorites, we've got some ideas.

Sources indicate that A lot of dystopian novels are referred to as "speculative fiction," which means that the scenario laid out by the author could conceivably happen in real life ... so, let's hope that Nana Kwame Adjei-Brenyah's novel "Chain-Gang All-Stars" doesn't come to pass. Released in 2023, this novel imagines a world where the incarceration system in the United States is, somehow, even worse than it is in our reality — in that prisoners are allowed to enroll in a program called CAPE, which stands for "Criminal Action Penal Entertainment." Not only are the inmates in CAPE constantly monitored (with their every move broadcast to hungry audiences), they're also sent across the country to constantly participate in gladiator matches against each other that are, you guessed it, televised as well. The book's title comes from the reimagined version of a traditional "chain gang," where the prisoner-gladiators are called "Links" and given two options to leave: either they're High Freed, meaning released, or Low Freed, meaning killed.

Throughout "Chain-Gang All-Stars," we follow the Angola-Hammond Chain in the system and, more specifically, Hamara "Hurricane Staxxx" Stacker and Loretta "Blood Mama" Thurwar, the two female fighters in a secret relationship who open the book. As we move through the unsettling world Adjei-Brenyah concocted in "Chain-Gang All Stars," we follow a wide variety of prisoners participating in this gut-wrenching game ... and it's sort of impossible to not think of the "Hunger Games" franchise as you read it, albeit in a good way. After you wrap up all five "Hunger Games" books, check out "Chain-Gang All-Stars." (Nina Starner).

In a recent development, when it comes to seeing people die horrible deaths in death games televised for the entertainment of an oppressive ruling class, no book does it on a larger scale than Matt Dinniman's "Dungeon Crawler Carl." The book takes place after Earth has been taken over by an alien corporation that seeks to mine the planet for resources. Those who aren't killed during the initial invasion are then forced to compete in an intergalactic reality show program, an RPG-like "dungeon crawl" where they have to navigate various levels of a labyrinthian dungeon, each filled with increasingly dangerous monsters and scenarios.

What makes "Dungeon Crawler Carl" unique is how it blends together ridiculous video game and tabletop RPG logic with an unhealthy dose of pop culture references, the humor of a Douglas Adams book, and the brutality and social commentary about unchecked capitalism and authoritarianism of "The Hunger Games." Indeed, reading Dinniman's book and its follow-ups is like playing a fun RPG session, in that it's chaotic, messy, hilarious, and weird, all while packing a serious emotional punch full of heartbreak and cruel twists and turns. But rather than reveling in their misery, Dinniman's characters rage against the corporate machine in an effort to break it. What you end up with is a story about the necessity of resistance and the importance of community, both of which are themes that will resonate with "Hunger Games" fans. And did I mention it features an endlessly quotable talking cat? (Rafael Motamayor).

I don't think it's possible to have a conversation about young adult dystopian books and films like the "Hunger Games" stories without discussing "The Handmaid's Tale." Margaret Atwood's landmark 1980 book set a standard for dystopian narratives rivaled only by George Orwell's "1984," but Atwood's specificity is what makes her imagined world so terrifying — in that "The Handmaid's Tale" takes place in a world where a religious totalitarian regime oppresses women and queer people. Offred (meaning "of Fred"), our heroine, works as one of the titular handmaids, which means she's prized for her fertility and used as a "vessel" (that's putting it politely) for her Commander, Fred, to impregnate instead of his un-fertile wife. As Offred exists in Gilead (which forbids women from having quite literally any rights and punishes them with death if they even try to stray), we follow her every move in the novel, learning bits and pieces about her life before Gilead as June, a mother and wife with the freedom to live as she pleased.

According to recent reports, "The Handmaid's Tale" was adapted into a Hulu series in 2017, and while I do think Elisabeth Moss did an incredible job playing Offred, the show ran through Atwood's book by the end of Season 1 and kept its wheels spinning for, in my opinion, far too long (although it at least gets its final message right.) If you haven't read Atwood's book but are familiar with its well-known red costumes and overall vibe, I couldn't possibly recommend it more. Its prose is beautiful, its subject matter is terrifying, and it's a clear precursor to and inspiration for the stories found in the "Hunger Games" franchise. (Nina Starner).

According to recent reports, though certainly not as dark in tone as "The Hunger Games," the pop culture celebration that is author Ernest Cline's "Ready Player One" is an oddly fitting companion piece for fans of the world Suzanne Collins built. One could even look at it as a bit of a palette cleanser, albeit one that still scratches a similar itch.

For those not familiar, the book takes place in 2044 and focuses on Wade Watts, who spends his days in the virtual utopia known as the OASIS. Wade's devoted his life to studying the puzzles hidden within this world's digital confines, themselves based on their creator's fixation on pop culture — with the promise of massive power and fortune to whoever can unlock them.

Recent findings suggest that "Ready Player One" is jam-packed with pop culture references and is lighthearted in a lot of ways. However, it's also terribly dystopian, as the OASIS is not only people's sole escape from the harsh realities of the outside world, there's very little person-to-person communication anymore outside of the virtual space. Beyond that, the rush to solve the puzzles and nab the fortune results in a deadly game for Wade and many others, which is where the "Hunger Games" of it all comes in.

Steven Spielberg's 2018 movie adaptation left a lot to be desired for many fans and, yes, a "Ready Player Two" movie was in the works in 2021, though it's yet to materialize. Setting the film aside, the novel remains a true gem filled with wonderful world building, fully-realized characters, and just a dash of "kill or be killed" to make the whole thing extra exciting, elevating it beyond the barrage of references it might have otherwise been. (Ryan Scott).

Sources indicate that the funny thing about Pierce Brown's "Red Rising" series is that the first book in the still-ongoing saga is very much a "Hunger Games" riff ... until it's not. Set in a distant future where humanity has been rigidly split into various genetically modified castes that determine a person's role in society, the story follows Darrow, a young Martian "red" whose wife is murdered by the ruling "gold" regime, sending him on a quest for revenge that ultimately spans the entire solar system. But before the sweeping space opera can begin, Darrow infiltrates the gold caste and must survive the Institute, a deadly school where young people are violently set against one another in not-so-simulated combat and conquest.

Sources indicate that those who enjoyed the blend of youthful angst, action, sci-fi world-building, and dystopian politics of "The Hunger Games" will take quickly and easily to "Red Rising," which offers a similar flavor with a harsher, more masculine edge. However, starting with the second book "Golden Son" and continuing into later installments, Brown takes things in a wholly fresh direction, turning his Suzanne Collins riff into the kind of sprawling, detailed, intense, and morally murky epic that would make Frank Herbert and George R.R. Martin proud. This is the perfect stepping stone for "Hunger Games" fans hoping to branch out into a different flavor of science fiction. It's familiar enough, until it is suddenly, and brutally, not. (Jacob Hall).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that spoilers for Disney's Hexed are ahead! You can catch the movie in theaters now.

Sources indicate that disney’s newest animated film, Hexed, is all about witches. At least, that’s what I expected it to be about from all the teasers and trailers released to promote the film. For the most part, Hexed does make good on that promise. However, by the time the credits started to roll, I couldn’t help but wonder if I just watched the origin story of a latest Disney princess.

Let me back up a bit, though. Hexed centers on Billie Doe, a mischievous high school student with a heart of gold who discovers she has magical powers while trying to evade her principal, who is going to expel her. Back at home, Billie opens a portal to Hexe, the magic-filled world where witches and wizards live. It’s there that she meets the Queen of Hexe, who just so happens to be her grandmother. Now, I’m not an expert on royal lineage, but I’m pretty sure being the granddaughter of the queen makes you a princess.

Sources indicate that here’s the thing: becoming an official Disney princess is a lot more complicated than it sounds. There are rules and requirements a character must meet before they’re even considered for the coronation. The big three are (via Movieweb): being the lead or co-lead in the movie, having a pet sidekick, being human (sorry, Nala), and having some connection to royalty or making a heroic decision (in the case of Mulan). However, even meeting all four requirements doesn’t guarantee a character a Disney crown. Just look at Frozen’s Anna and Elsa. Though, in the famous sisters’ case, Disney considers them to be more popular on their own than they would be as part of the official lineup.

All of this begs the question: Is Billie a Disney princess? She’s definitely the lead of the movie. In a way, she has two sidekicks, one in the form of the cat, Beef Roger Crummchuk, and the other in the form of the bewitched cauldron, Bucket. She may be a witch, but she’s a human witch. And not only does she have a connection to royalty through her grandmother and later her mom after she assumes the rightful role of Queen as Hexe, but she also makes a heroic move to save the world of Hexe.

Billie From Hexed Has Just Landed At Disney Parks, But The Directors Already Have Bigger Ideas.

It has been revealed that there’s no doubt that Billie has met the big four requirements. However, there is one more lesser-known requirement that has to be met for the House of Mouse to consider a character an official princess: the movie has to be a hit. In fact, the success of a movie has to extend well past its release to ensure a princess keeps her title — just look at The Hunchback of Notre Dame’s Esmerelda, who used to be in the official lineup and now is not.

Sources indicate that unfortunately, the early box office numbers aren’t looking too great for Hexed. I’m not too worried about Billie’s princess status, though, since plenty of recent Disney original movies have found their audiences after they’ve been released and made available for those with a Disney+ subscription. At least, that’s what I’m telling myself because I really want Billie to be Disney’s first pink-haired princess!

#154574. Lucia’s Rise: ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Forces Gamers to Grow Up—and Punishes Them With Narrative Consequences If They Refuse

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1854 w)

Lucia’s Rise: ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Forces Gamers to Grow Up—and Punishes Them With Narrative Consequences If They Refuse

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the last 25 years, nearly every noxious gamer stereotype had a home in Grand Theft Auto.
  • In a recent development, this, for the most part, suited Grand Theft Auto’s publisher just fine.
  • In a recent development, but with Grand Theft Auto VI, something has changed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the last 25 years, nearly every noxious gamer stereotype had a home in Grand Theft Auto. Juvenile, sexist, crass, embarrassing—people could accuse the games of being these things because the allegations were, in part, true. Beginning with 2001’s Grand Theft Auto III, the series began giving players the freedom to wreak havoc across satirical renditions of US cities. It was an amazing technical feat that only grew more impressive with each subsequent Grand Theft Auto game—and harder to appreciate the more those cities were filled with dick jokes and sex workers.

In a recent development, this, for the most part, suited Grand Theft Auto’s publisher just fine. What business did the company have calling itself Rockstar Games if it cared what a bunch of prudes thought?

In a recent development, but with Grand Theft Auto VI, something has changed. And the game’s staggering launch-day revenue—$3.79 billion—suggests that this change was a welcome one.

According to recent reports, rockstar has executed an astonishing about-face in Grand Theft Auto VI, choosing to build a game around a couple depicted with aching sincerity—from their car-boosting meet-cute to the desperate stickups they commit, with the player’s help. Jason Duval (played by Dylan Rourke) and Lucia Caminos (Manni L. Perez) are a modern-day Bonnie and Clyde, out of options and on the run, hoping they can land a score significant enough to turn things around.

This earnestness is fresh for Grand Theft Auto, which historically has had a deep love for pushing buttons. (Its sister series, the Western Red Dead Redemption, has less of a problem with heart-on-the-sleeve storytelling.) Lucia, especially, is new. She’s the first woman you can play as in the series, and by the transitive property, she’s also the first woman that Grand Theft Auto has ever had to take seriously. Doing so changes the entire shape of the series.

It has been revealed that until now, Grand Theft Auto has never really thought much of women. True, the games have never thought much of anyone; Rockstar traffics in a nihilistic comedy that lies somewhere between South Park and a Verhoeven film, a dim view of the United States where everyone sucks. But women, usually, have sucked the most. They’ve been the butts of countless jokes; in the Grand Theft Auto universe, they’ve been nags and drags and sex workers secondary to the men that the games were about. Grand Theft Auto III, a game that barely has a plot, begins with main character Clyde’s girlfriend betraying him after a heist, shooting him and calling him “small time” before running off with the take. It doesn’t get much better from there.

So yes: Lucia is a huge pivot for the series, especially because Grand Theft Auto VI doesn’t trust players with her right away. After a brief prologue in which a desperate stickup goes wrong, Lucia is sent to jail and players begin the game as her boyfriend Jason Duval. In addition to doing odd jobs for a small-time crime boss (Stephen Root) and hanging out with your pal (Bobby Moynihan), players have to choose: Are they going to be a good boyfriend? Rockstar Games know they might be making a big ask of their audience, so they slow-roll it. Before Lucia gets out of jail, the game suggests to the player, maybe fix the stairs? Or get a haircut? Buy her a necklace?

Recent findings suggest that in the days since the game came out, many have noted how amusing it is that Grand Theft Auto VI has made caring about your girlfriend one of its first challenges. The game’s “Lucia will appreciate this” notification is its first viral meme, and the source of both incel crashouts (“woke slop … so obvious it was made by women”) and earnest appreciation. (One of the first clips to spread online was of streamer Stable Ronaldo painting Jason and Lucia's bedroom one color before recoiling in horror: What if she hates that shade?).

Industry observers note that lucia is a destabilizing event not just for gamers, but for Grand Theft Auto—a damning yet fascinating example of gaming culture’s priorities on its biggest stage. GTA has always been a series of warring ambitions: violent Rube Goldberg machine, Karl Ove Knausgaard–esque obsession with quotidian details, and thrilling Hollywood blockbuster all in one. These disparate aims are often in conflict with one another, and one way to read the series’ heretofore exclusively male focus is as an attempt to thread this needle. By tossing all of its commentary under the carpet of “satire," Rockstar can also use a veneer of meanness to argue that the games’ misogyny is actually an intentional lambasting, much like everything else in GTA.

But taking a woman seriously, and making her colead with a male character, requires an entire rethinking of what Grand Theft Auto is. “It’s a product of the story we’re trying to tell,” Grand Theft Auto VI codirector Rob Nelson noted when asked by The Guardian if this is the first Grand Theft Auto to encourage empathy from players. “We’ve tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.”.

This is an extremely roundabout way of saying that, in this Grand Theft Auto, Rockstar asks gamers to grow up—and punishes them with narrative consequences if they don’t take the game up on the offer.

Sources indicate that the funny thing about Grand Theft Auto VI’s gamified empathy is that, like everything else in a video game, it has to teach the player how to accomplish that goal. The game does this through prompting players to do chores, but also through Jason’s characterization. Throughout the game, Rockstar has to convey what its writers believe a well-adjusted man looks like—or at least what constitutes a man well-adjusted enough to earn the respect of a woman like Lucia, who walks out on him when he tries to exclude her from some of his more dangerous criminal activities.

Sources indicate that to that end, there are an abundance of moments in the game where Jason demonstrates the virtues of being respectful and maintaining boundaries, several of which are a departure from GTA series norms. There are no sex workers in the game anymore (though there are strip clubs). While Jason and Lucia can break up depending on the player’s choices, there are no other options for committed or casual romance.

Sources indicate that the money you steal is ostensibly for Jason and Lucia to use together: so they can get away and start over with their young son, who’s right now entrusted to a relative. Casual conversations between strangers players meet on the road make Jason’s respectful nature both a point and a punchline. There’s one man who’s looking for his missing wife after a night of partying. When he starts to brag about her sexual dexterity, Jason interjects to say, “Hey. Let’s draw a line, bud.”.

According to recent reports, in some ways, this is all rather embarrassing—though in a different way than the weapons-grade sexism of Grand Theft Autos past. One ought to feel a twinge of shame while marveling at any entertainment franchise for including a woman. Yet Grand Theft Auto VI is being graded on a curve. It has a near-perfect Metacritic score in large part for its depiction of Lucia, and for Jason’s relationship to her. The context speaks to a state of arrested development, both in Grand Theft Auto and in big-budget games writ large.

Industry observers note that none of this changes the fact that Lucia really is one of the most well-realized video game characters in a digital city unlike any other. But perhaps her inclusion is less an apology for GTA’s past, and more of a concession to how out of step the series had become with the culture. Because if you’re meant to have empathy for one character, the natural next question is, “Well, what about everyone else?".

Rockstar’s maniacal pursuit of verisimilitude goes a long way here. The game’s animations are so realistic that in GTA VI, shooting unarmed civilians is legitimately unsettling. It’s also disincentivized by a “criminal profile” rating that will mark your character “irredeemable” if you engage in too much wanton violence. (This is not a “game over”—it merely locks players out of achieving a happy ending unless they restart from before their murder spree.) These sorts of limits have become another reliable source of outrage directed at the game, with rage baiters drumming up controversy over Rockstar’s decision to, for example, not permit players to shoot up a nightclub.

Recent findings suggest that this is the tricky reality of encouraging empathy for “those who want to,” as Nelson put it. Rockstar has certain intentions, but so do players—and managing both is the great challenge of making any video game. Empathy is a shock to GTA’s system and to the audience alike.

Recent findings suggest that replicating humanity with computer software is a daunting and costly task, and one that only Rockstar seems to have the limitless resources to pursue. Those resources—the luxury to work as long as necessary to complete Grand Theft Auto VI, and the obscene amount of money it cost (our only solid figure is “less than $1.5 billion”)—are rapidly dwindling in the video game business, as all available tech funding is vacuumed up by AI companies and private equity loots what’s left. Grand Theft Auto VI may very well be one of one: the most expensive game ever and the last of its kind, the peak of Rockstar’s ambition and also of every massive-budget video game. Here, at the end of everything, the biggest of video games has finally decided that it’s time to try empathy. And for a woman, even, should gamers choose (and not all will).

It’s a bit of an indictment of the billion-dollar video game industry that the most expensive game in history is also the first major game to commit to a realistic heterosexual relationship. Grand Theft Auto VI deserves many of the accolades it instantly garnered upon release, but the nature of its accomplishment is not yet fully understood. It’s possible that what Rockstar has built is less a monument to video games’ potential than a magnificent funeral pyre, a testament to how things might’ve turned out if Rockstar’s priorities—and those of everyone chasing after its vision of what video games could be—were just a little bit different.

  • Sources indicate that the report also states that GTA 6 had an impact on sales for some of 2026's other major releases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we might have to stop saying something sold like hotcakes and start saying something sold like Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar's latest has sold about as well as we expected, with estimates after only one week putting sales at over 50 million copies. That number will only go up in the weeks and months to come, especially if a fresh GTA Online mode and a PC version are eventually declared, as rumored.

According to estimates from Alinea Analytics, GTA 6 has sold 53 million copies in the week following the game's release on Nov. 19. That equates to $4.7 billion in revenue. By comparison, GTA 5 only sold 29 million copies in its entire first month. (It has since gone on to sell more than 230 million copies.) Other stats from the report reveal that nearly 7 million players have logged more than 50 hours in the game, with around 250,000 logging more than 100 hours.

Sources indicate that the report also states that GTA 6 had an impact on sales for some of 2026's other major releases. On PlayStation, sales of several games (including 007 First Light​​​​​​​, Resident Evil Requiem, and Marvel's Wolverine) fell 34% during the week of GTA 6's release. ​​​​​​​Alinea Analytics points out​​​​​​​ that this isn't all GTA 6's fault, as typical sales decay for these titles was also in full swing. Interestingly, sales did actually go up slightly in the week before the game's release, possibly because some players​​​​​​​ ​​​​​​​bought a PS5 and picked up a game or two​​​​​​​ to hold them over until GTA 6's release.​​​​​​​.

Of the more than 50 million copies of GTA 6 sold, more than 75% were sold for PlayStation 5.​​​​​​​ The report also highlights that Xbox sales have continued to decline​​​​​​​ in the days following the game's release. This suggests​​​​​​​ that Rockstar and PlayStation's marketing deal has been a massive success. Prior to the game's release, GTA 6 had been heavily promoted as playing best​​​​​​​ on Sony's console. Granted, PlayStation does at the moment hold roughly 75% of the console market, making GTA 6 sales roughly proportional to its market share​​​​​​​. Fresh off the success of GTA 6 on PlayStation 5, Sony has already struck a similar marketing deal with CD Projekt Red for future releases, including The Witcher 4.

PC players have been left out of the fun so far, with no official word on a PC release for GTA 6. That hasn't stopped hackers from trying to make their own, with builds making speedy progress after an Xbox executable file was leaked to the public, kick-starting a race to create an unofficial PC port​​​​​​​. Hopefully, we'll hear official word on a PC release and multiplayer sometime in 2027.​​​​​​​.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is now available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, "The Hunger Games" franchise is back with a story fans have been waiting a very long time for. "Sunrise on the Reaping" is the darkest movie in "The Hunger Games" series, flashing back to the famed games in which Haymitch Abernathy won. Originally played by Woody Harrelson, that character is a fan-favorite, but this movie does a lot of work to help fill in crucial elements of his character, played this time by Joseph Zada.

It has been revealed that "Sunrise on the Reaping" takes place on the "Hunger Games" timeline 24 years before the events of the first movie. It follows sixteen-year-old Haymitch from District 12, beginning on the morning of the reaping for the 50th Annual Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, the biggest Games yet with twice as many tributes. But Haymitch isn't the only classic character who gets more time to shine in this entry.

Plenty of "Hunger Games" characters return in this prequel in younger form, including Caesar Flickerman (played by Oscar winner Kieran Culkin) and Effie Trinket (played by Emmy nominee Elle Fanning). But they're not the only ones who will be familiar to fans of the series. There's also the matter of Mags Flanagan, a very important character in the history of both the books and the movies. Originally played by Lynn Cohen in "Catching Fire," she won the 11th Hunger Games and volunteered as tribute during the 75th games.

According to recent reports, this time around, the younger version of Cohen is played by actress Lili Taylor. The role is crucial, as Mags is the one who mentors Haymitch en route to his time in the games. But for those who feel Taylor looks familiar, there's a good reason for that: She's a great actress with one heck of a resume.

Lili Taylor got her start as an actress in the late '80s/early '90s, starring in movies such as "Mystic Pizza," "Say Anything," and "Born on the Fourth of July." She worked steadily throughout the '90s in movies, in addition to doing some television, including an episode of "The X-Files." Some of her other notable credits from this period include "Ransom" and "The Haunting.".

One of her earliest, big breakout roles came in the early 2000s on "Six Feet Under," one of the best HBO demonstrates of all time, as Lisa Kimmel. She also continued to work very steadily in movies during this period, earning credits in "Brooklyn's Finest" and "Public Enemies," among others. Though not often in the spotlight as a lead, Taylor tends to use her talents in memorable supporting roles.

The 2010s were particularly kind to Taylor. 2013's "The Conjuring" kicked off the biggest non-Marvel cinematic universe, and she had a major part to play as Carolyn Perron, one of the heads of the household at the center of that movie's haunting. It's arguably her most notable role to date. She reprised the role in "The Nun" and "The Conjuring: Last Rites." That same year, she also starred in "Hemlock Grove," one of the first original shows produced by Netflix.

Taylor has over 100 credits to her name so we can't possibly go over all of them, but some other titles viewers might recognize her from include "The Maze Runner: The Scorch Trials," "Leatherface," HBO's "Perry Mason," "Outer Range," "Fear Street: Prom Queen," and most recently Marvel's "Daredevil: Born Again," where she played Marge McCaffrey.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A security researcher has discovered a publicly exposed database containing approximately two billion credentials. The database was neither password-protected nor encrypted.

The scariest part of it is around 400,000 documents came from separate folders for individual victims, creating a detailed profile with all the personal data needed to “own that person” ….

Cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler says that the database contains a huge array of information, including login details for Tor .onion addresses used to access the dark web.

I also observed thousands of Tor .onion addresses associated with account names and passwords. The Tor .onion services are generally categorized as part of the dark web, and these credentials could potentially provide access to private forums, marketplaces, communication platforms, or other hidden services. While .onion accounts alone do not imply criminal or malicious activity, it is estimated that as much as 60% of dark web sites host illegal material and illicit activities. This is the first time I have seen a large number of dark web accounts in breached credentials. It should be noted that legitimate organizations, journalists, whistleblower platforms, and news organizations also operate .onion services to provide anonymity and bypass censorship.

But the most frightening aspect of it is separate folders for individual victims containing all of the information needed for identity theft.

Fowler told Wired that this data appears to have been obtained through advanced malware.

Sources indicate that the “scariest” thing in the database, Fowler says, was around 400,000 documents that appeared to come from “more advanced malware” compiling information about individual victims […] that create a detailed profile of an individual and their digital life. “If you had that, you own that person,” Fowler says.

There’s no information about the specific sources of the data, but it seems likely to be aggregated from a range of data breaches. Fowler contacted the hosting tech giant to have the database removed, but it’s not known how many people may have had access to it.

Recent findings suggest that the best protection is to use a password manager like Apple’s Passwords app to ensure you have strong, unique passwords for each individual website and service you use, with two-factor authentication enabled wherever possible. When given the choice of 2FA code delivery, you should always opt for an authenticator app rather than a text message to protect yourself against SIM-swap attacks.

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth has Brad Pitt and director David Fincher continuing what Quentin Tarantino started on Once Upon a Time… In Hollywood on the 2026 movie schedule. When CinemaBlend spoke to one of Pitt's co-stars, she recalled how the Fight Club actor handled his longtime collaborator’s reputation on set.

It has been revealed that after previously working together on Se7en, Fight Club and The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, Brad Pitt and David Fincher reteamed for the fourth time for Cliff Booth after getting Tarantino’s blessing to adapt his script. Pitt is a veteran of Fincher’s relentless use of takes, and Carla Gugino told us about one time on set when Pitt commented on it. In her words to CinemaBlend:.

Industry observers note that I just remember at one point we were doing the master, and Brad just really sweetly looked over at the guy who was standing there as the valet who'd been there for so many hours, and he looked over, and he was like, ‘Don't worry, you will go home.’ It was really sweet. Gugino plays Toni Peters, a former lover of Cliff Booth, whom he runs into while working with her husband, Charlie Peters (played by Scott Caan). During a scene where they talk outside a tennis club, Gugino recalled the scene requiring a lot of takes because it “involved so many elements” like a crane and cars coming and going.

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is presently showing on IMAX screens and will be available to stream with a Netflix subscription starting on December 23. You can check out what the reviews are saying before seeing Pitt and Fincher’s latest collaboration.

  • It's been a funny season, and it's been a heartfelt season at times, particularly when the show killed Kenny (again) and decided to replace him with none other than a kid version of Randy (complete with mustache).
  • Industry observers note that in the finale, "City Endings," the town of South Park (renamed this season as South America) is hit with major power outages that disrupt the town's "GTA VI" gametime.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"South Park" has been on a roll recently. When the show finally left behind its Mr.-Garrison-as-Trump allegory and stopped doing endless specials (even if most of those were fantastic), it found its stride again in Season 28, which took on AI and deepfakes in the funniest way possible. Then, Season 29 took on everything from the data centers, to "looksmaxxing" and "aura farming" in a hilarious "Backrooms" parody, to club sports in a great "Heated Rivalry" parody, to the US beef shortage, and more.

It's been a funny season, and it's been a heartfelt season at times, particularly when the show killed Kenny (again) and decided to replace him with none other than a kid version of Randy (complete with mustache). It has even been a romantic season, with the Tweek and Craig romance-focused episode. What "South Park" usually isn't, however, is scary. That changed with the Season 29 finale, which delivered the scariest TV scene of 2026 — twice.

Industry observers note that in the finale, "City Endings," the town of South Park (renamed this season as South America) is hit with major power outages that disrupt the town's "GTA VI" gametime. It is part of a conspiracy involving secret deals the government made with billionaire weenies. At the same time, there's paranoia involving supposed Chinese spies and possible cyberattacks from that country.

In a recent development, in the middle of all this, Cartman, Stan, and Kyle are also haunted by visions of the late Kenny, who died after being blown up by an e-bike in the season's premiere. Except this is not just Kenny, but a zombified version that haunts the boys in the form of horrific ghouls that even infiltrate "GTA VI," like a spectre out of "The Ring.".

"South Park" has toyed with the horror genre before, usually body horror. There was the Michael Jackson parody with Mr. Jefferson slowly rotting away, for example, or the HumanCentipad. The Season 29 finale, however, features one of the wildest and most gruesome eldritch abominations in the nearly 30-year history of the show. It starts with several scenes of Kenny simply standing creepily in the background, stalking the boys as if to try and send a message.

"City Endings" is a legit horror episode, which is rare from the show that spent nearly a decade on a silly weed farm storyline. The image of Kenny just standing in the background, his face obscured by his hoodie but with bright eyes just shining like Pennywise in "It," is already quite disturbing and terrifying. Then, when the boys finally catch up to Kenny, who leads them to the cemetery and to his own grave, he shows off his gruesome zombie face and starts dissolving like that guy in "Poltergeist," in excruciatingly disturbing detail, before exploding in a pool of blood.

In a recent development, it's enough to make your skin crawl, but it's not even the scariest scene of the episode. That climax comes in later, while the boys are playing "GTA VI" at Butters' house. We see the zombie Kenny monster with long spiky teeth, deranged eyes and elongated limbs with claws crawling out of the TV like Samara Morgan from "The Ring." It is the stuff of pure nightmares, and by far the scariest scene in 2026 television.

This Year, Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Is Doing Broadway a Little Differently

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1395 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This year’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is going to look a bit different.
  • The result is an epic 10-minute medley, introduced by Julianne Hough, who will star in Damn Yankees on Broadway this spring, featuring nine beloved Broadway demonstrates: The Book of Mormon, Chicago, Disney’s Aladdin, Hamilton, The Lost Boys, Rent, Richard O’Brien’s The Rocky Horror Show, Schmigadoon!, and—what else?—Wicked.
  • Industry observers note that the mastermind behind the mega-medley is none other than Tom Kitt, the Tony-, Emmy-, Grammy-, and Pulitzer Prize–winning composer behind Next to Normal, If/Then, and Almost Famous.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This year’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is going to look a bit different. First, the threat of severe weather has prompted Macy’s to reschedule the event until Saturday, beginning at 8:30 a.m. ET. But even before the forecast turned, there was a big change: While in the past, viewers would enjoy five or so of the best performances from the current Broadway season, this year, there’s only one big Broadway number. But don’t fret, theater folk. For the milestone occasion of the parade’s 100th anniversary, the powers that be at NBC and Macy’s have put a new spin on their tried-and-true formula, gathering the Broadway community for one supersized performance, featuring more shows and performers than ever before.

The result is an epic 10-minute medley, introduced by Julianne Hough, who will star in Damn Yankees on Broadway this spring, featuring nine beloved Broadway demonstrates: The Book of Mormon, Chicago, Disney’s Aladdin, Hamilton, The Lost Boys, Rent, Richard O’Brien’s The Rocky Horror Show, Schmigadoon!, and—what else?—Wicked.

Industry observers note that the mastermind behind the mega-medley is none other than Tom Kitt, the Tony-, Emmy-, Grammy-, and Pulitzer Prize–winning composer behind Next to Normal, If/Then, and Almost Famous. Kitt is no stranger to writing a significant production number, having cowritten the Tony Awards opening number “Bigger!,” performed by host Neil Patrick Harris with lyrics by Lin-Manuel Miranda in 2013, among other ambitious musical endeavors. Despite his previous experience, a 10-minute, nine-show medley presented a unique set of challenges the composer had yet to tackle.

In a recent development, A total of 133 people are performing in the medley—114 Broadway cast members, 17 dancers, a child actor, and Hough. On top of that, more than 125 other Broadway professionals—including stage managers, wardrobe supervisors, and hair and makeup teams—are on site to facilitate the production, bringing the total number of people involved to well over 250.

“Most important to me in doing something like this—to celebrate this community, this beautiful community that I’m so lucky to be a part of,” Kitt tells me. “Everyone who’s participating, you want them to feel happy and excited about what they’re doing.”.

A little over a month ago, Kitt and creative producer Sarah O’Gleby got to work figuring out how to make a cohesive musical number out of nine very different shows. He wrote the first draft of the arrangement over the course of a few days. “It was way too long,” he says. That might be because Kitt had to figure out how to connect these disparate shows musically while also finding room for Easter eggs for theater fans: musical nods to shows that might not otherwise be featured in the medley, including Anything Goes, The Music Man, A Chorus Line, and Kitt’s personal favorite, Into the Woods, whose music kicks things off.

“Into the Woods was one of those reveals that made me want to write for the theater,” he tells me. “The downbeat of the prologue is one of the most beautiful musical gestures; every time I hear it, I get goosebumps. So that was really special and vital for me to get to plug into, and there are so many others.”.

Surprisingly, it will be Kitt’s first time attending the parade in person. “The parade has meant so much to me,” he says. “I’ve watched it for years. I’ve taped it. I’m lucky enough to have highlights that have been a part of it. I think that celebrating that relationship and celebrating the history of Broadway and being able to spotlight so many important shows and artists just feels very exciting and gratifying.”.

“I’m a tiny little person, but I love to do really major things,” states O’Gleby. A former performer on the West End, O’Gleby moved to the States almost two decades ago to pursue a career as a Broadway performer, dancing in revivals of Brigadoon and How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying. Now she choreographs Broadway productions like Shucked and, most recently, Pink’s widely celebrated Tony Awards opening number. Given her Broadway bona fides, she’s also intimately familiar with the magic of the parade. “I was lucky to perform on the parade as a Broadway girl and the associate choreographer and dance captain on highlights that I was in,” she says. “It was so wonderfully American.”.

The first of two rehearsals took place Friday afternoon at Pier59 Studios at Chelsea Piers. Around 4 p.m., as the sun began to set over the Hudson River, Broadway performers from different demonstrates practiced the medley. O’Gleby, wearing silver leather pants and clutching a God mic, was charged with organizing the chaos and managing the more than 100 Broadway performers in the room. Standing offstage between a broomstick and a red Les Mis flag, I could still see traces of green makeup on the face of Wicked’s current Elphaba, Keri René Fuller. Most of the performers gathered had a show of their own to perform in just a few hours, but that didn’t stop them from giving it their all in rehearsal, onstage and off, cheering the other productions along as each got its moment in the spotlight.

It has been revealed that case in point: At the end of the rehearsal, the whole room erupted into cheers for the original cast members from Rent—including original Angel, Tony winner Wilson Jermaine Heredia, and original Joanne, Fredi Walker—who are gathering to perform “Seasons of Love” in the parade. (During the rehearsal, Aladdin’s current Genie, Sherri Shepherd, couldn’t help but mouth along to the words of the seminal song.) “It was that moment of why we’re a part of this community,” O’Gleby says, nearly choking up. “Everyone in the room—stage managers, costume, I mean everybody in the room—the way they were applauding these original cast members and what they gave to all of us as a community, really all over the world, it was incredible.”.

It has been revealed that at the second rehearsal, on Monday night outside on 34th Street beneath Macy’s giant turkey, the mood remained high even as the temperatures dropped. By 11 p.m., performers were bundled in winter jackets, sweatshirts, and leg warmers, with their character shoes still on. They hugged one another for warmth and jumped up and down, kicking their feet to stay loose between setups. Margaret Cho, who stars as the Narrator in The Rocky Horror Show, danced “The Time Warp” with her Chihuahua, Lucia, tucked into a pouch in her jacket, the dog’s head peeking out.

Industry observers note that for O’Gleby, a smooth Monday-night rehearsal means setting each show up for success come Saturday morning and making sure all nine demonstrates are “represented in the most powerful and clear storytelling way that we can,” she states. “This is a huge moment for these shows to sell lots of tickets so everyone gets to keep making their magic every night. And so it’s notable to me that each team gets to communicate what they need and what they think would really make their show shine.”.

On Wednesday afternoon, Macy's confirmed that “after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration,” a disappointing piece of news for those who build their holiday around the annual event.

Recent findings suggest that this is only the fourth time in history that the parade hasn't been held on Thanksgiving: In 1942, 1943, and 1944 it was canceled completely as its trademark giant balloons were repurposed as part of the World War II effort. Compared to those years, a move to Saturday seems manageable, O’Gleby says. “The weather will be what it will be, but we will delight in that and deliver the best.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in September, Apple held a photography exhibition in Newly introduced York City to show off the iPhone 18 Pro camera. Now, an image of the Bugaboo Mountains from that exhibit, shot by photographer Jimmy Chin, is included in TIME’s Top 100 Photos.

Recent findings suggest that TIME publishes its Top 100 Photos list each year. The list showcases the pictures that the TIME Photo Department determines best capture that particular year.

The essence of TIME’s Photos of the Year, selected by our photo editors and presented below, is the authentic, sometimes staggering, reality captured by photojournalism. Someone was there. A news photographer lifted a viewfinder, pressed a button, and captured an instant happening in front of them.

Chin’s image was shot in Bugaboo Provincial Park, Canada, on iPhone 18 Pro. He explained that a traditional production creates a layer of separation between the photographer and the subject, with equipment, crew, and all the moving parts of a shoot. Shooting on iPhone 18 Pro meant that he could create a more intimate environment, allowing for a sense of comfort and spontaneity that comes through in the images.

Image Courtesy of Apple (as featured in the What Holds Us exhibition).

Chin’s goal was to capture the intersection of human ambition and the pursuit of wonder against the backdrop of a timeless natural landscape.

It has been revealed that “The resolution and the sharpness on iPhone 18 Pro surprised me. I could shoot a few inches of rock and ice, or a massive panorama, and trust it would hold at size. That is what this work needed. It also meant I carried almost nothing. In the mountains, everything you carry is a decision. I was not thinking about gear. I was thinking about what was in front of me.”.

Apple’s “What Holds Us” exhibit ran in New York City in September, featuring work from photographers Alex Prager, Jack Davison, and Jimmy Chin, with each artist using the iPhone 18 Pro to explore the “people, places, and ideas that connect and ground humanity.” Kathy Ryan, the former longtime director of photography for The New York Times Magazine, curated the exhibition.

The exhibit is now headed to London, where it will open to the public on December 4, from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. It will also be open from Saturday, December 12 through Sunday, December 13, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.

💡 Key Takeaways
