  • According to recent reports, in this TV spot, Magneto (Ian McKellen) tries to telekinetically rip off Doom's mask — it is made of metal, after all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that marvel Comics fans know Doctor Victor von Doom is scarcely ever seen without his iron mask — a mask that hides his supposedly horribly scarred face. But with Marvel Studios choosing former Tony Stark actor Robert Downey Jr. to play Doom in the upcoming "Avengers" movies "Doomsday" and "Secret Wars," there's been an expectation that Doom's mask coming off will be a jaw dropping moment.

Now, Chris Evans has claimed that Doom wears his mask for the entirety of "Doomsday." But that could only mean he'll keep the mask on until "Secret Wars." Even then, there's the chance that Doom is so disfigured that his face isn't even recognizable as RDJ. A latest TV spot for "Doomsday" does suggest Doom has his scarred face, while also teasing we're eventually going to see exactly what's under his mask ... but not yet.

According to recent reports, in this TV spot, Magneto (Ian McKellen) tries to telekinetically rip off Doom's mask — it is made of metal, after all. But Doom does not restrict himself to the laws of science. There's evidently a magical seal on the mask (note there appear to be runic designs across Doom's costume), because glowing green tendrils extend out from Doom's hood and grab the mask, slamming it back onto Doom's face. A brief glimpse of Doom's face, visible through the mask's eyeholes, indicates hints of pale macerated skin and scar tissue.

In the "Fantastic Four" comics, it was originally mentioned that Doom suffered his scars during an experiment in college. A machine he built to contact the "nether world" (later revealed to be an attempt to reach his mother's damned soul) exploded in his face, leaving him scarred.

Now, Doom's co-creator Jack Kirby intended that Doom actually only had a thin facial scar — but Doom's ego can't stand even that small imperfection. Later "Fantastic Four" writer/artist John Byrne melded the two ideas. The machine explosion only slightly damaged Doom's face, but then Victor — convinced his face was already ruined — put his freshly forged mask on before it cooled, and that is why he has a horribly scarred face.

According to recent reports, the greatest source of Doom's torment is completely self-inflicted. The exemplary 1989 "Doctor Strange and Doctor Doom: Triumph and Torment" goes with Byrne's interpretation. When Doom seeks out the wisdom of the wizard named the Aged Genghis, the sorcerer alludes to Doom's "minor disfigurement." We then see Doom's (barely scarred) face as Victor lashes out at the insult.

It's unclear what origin "Doomsday" will go with, if any of them. Marketing suggests the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Doom will be driven by a lost wife and child, not his mother. What is clear from this TV spot is that Marvel fans can expect to see Doom and Magneto — the two greatest villains of Marvel Comics — clash onscreen. Doom's wizardry here refutes the obvious conclusion that Magneto wins easily because he controls metal and Doom is concealed inside metal armor.

"He is pain, he is extinction," Magneto declares, setting up Doom's famous third person double entendre: "I am Doom!" Ian McKellen's Magneto was the first villain of the Marvel movie boom that kicked off with 2000's "X-Men." Bringing him back to face (and presumably fall to) Doom is some classic carnival barker marketing that would make Stan Lee proud.

"Avengers: Doomsday" is set for theatrical release on December 18, 2026.

CAD images of the iPhone 18e, mentioned to come from a previously reliable source, have shown a rather odd latest design for the camera bump.

If accurate, it would represent a substantial change from its predecessor, which simply has a single lens protruding without a surrounding bump or plateau ….

The iPhone 17e was rolled out in March with a design unchanged from last year’s iPhone 16e. While the camera did get some feature enhancements, including the ability to store depth information for portrait photos, the physical camera design remained the same.

Recent findings suggest that the current model has a single lens protruding directly from the casing with a flush-mounted flashlight next to it. Engadget reports on CAD images showing a very different approach with next year’s iPhone 18e.

The renders show an almost square camera bump measuring about 28 mm by 35 mm that houses the single rear camera, the LED flash and the rear microphone.

The site doesn’t share the images, but says that the camera bump looks similar to that of the M5 iPad Pro, shown below.

It’s unclear what might have prompted the change of design, especially as the site’s Filipe Espósito claims he’s also seen CAD models for the standard model iPhone 18 or the iPhone Air 2, neither of which adopt it.

Previous reports have suggested that the only spec change with the iPhone 18e over its predecessor will be performance improvements thanks to the A20 chip.

Kerry Kennedy is not in Milan on political business, but it’s hard to rein in the enthusiasm of some Americans following the 2026 midterm elections. Democrats won decisive majorities in both the House and Senate, along with 24 of the 36 governors elections held this month. It was a blue tsunami. Kennedy—a lawyer and human rights activist born in 1959 to dynasty Democrats Robert and Ethel Kennedy—is in a celebratory mood.

She’s in town for one night only to attend a charity dinner in support of her foundation, the Robert & Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Center. But first she sits down with Vanity Fair Italia, and over the course of our chat, she takes her beloved poodle, Scamper, for a short walk; sips two cappuccinos (strictly decaf), one of them iced (she apologizes to the Italians present); eats some gianduiotti chocolates; gestures animatedly; and smooths her very blonde hair.

But above all, she never stops smiling: “In America you can only go so far in the attempt to avoid the rule of law and erode democracy,” she says, making clear that her political statements are delivered in her personal capacity, “because at a certain point, even if you’re the most powerful and the richest man there, democracy will bring you down. From left: Robert Kennedy Jr., Joseph P Kennedy Jr., Tory Kennedy, and Kerry Kennedy on January 1, 1994.

Congress has the power of the purse, and now it’s going to exercise that power. But….

It has been revealed that he’s still the president for two more years. We didn’t get the White House.

Ethel Kennedy and daughter Kerry Kennedy circa 1979.

Who is your ideal candidate for the 2028 presidential election?

Anyone whose last name is Democrat.

Do you think [President Barack] Obama played a role in the Democrats’ success?

Obama is beloved. The only person who’s beloved more is Michelle [Obama]. And when I watched his speeches, he was so clear and concise about the differences between the Republicans and the Democrats, with his moral authority and his joy.

Recent findings suggest that you’ve talked about how your mother supported your father. Can you share an example of that?

My father was working for the Senate, and he was investigating organized crime’s infiltration of the Teamsters union, stealing pension funds from the rank-and-file Teamsters. There was a journalist from the Latest York Post who was also investigating, and somebody threw acid in his face. He was permanently blinded. A few days later, my mother got an anonymous letter saying, “Your children will be next.” She took her three oldest kids, put them in the back of her car, drove them to the Capitol, walked into the hearing room, and sat in the front row while daddy was interrogating Jimmy Hoffa, the head of the Teamsters.

Sources indicate that she was saying, “You’re not going to get to me through my children, and you’re not going to get to my husband through me. We are a fortress and we’re coming after you.” I don’t know how she grappled with the trauma.

Sources indicate that she needed to be there for us. She was an athlete. And if you feel physically mighty, it’s very helpful when you have to also be psychologically mighty. She would get up and go swimming, then horseback riding, sailing, and after a sail, she would go for a swim. She also had a very deep faith. Yes. In December, I’ll step down from being president of this organization. I’ll stay on the board and I’ll be president emeritus and I’ll still be involved, but I want to go to divinity school.

What lesson did you learn from your parents?

It has been revealed that when we were kids, when we would have a battle, and there were lots of battles, my father always did the same thing. He would bring two of us into a room. Were you a happy little girl before that day?

For us kids, it felt like we were part of something bigger.

Your latest book, which has just been published, is a biography of your mother: Ethel Kennedy: The Extraordinary Life and Bold Legacy. What kind of person was she?

My mother loved men. If you’re a woman, you’re great, and you’re her friend. But when a man was watching, it was incredible. Her whole life, that’s the way she was. When she was 96 and her mind was kind of in and out, I called her from my hotel in Milan and I remarked, “I’m here. Can I bring you anything? Do you want some limoncello or a bag of that beautiful spaghetti that they sell at the airport? What can I bring you from Italy?” And she answered, “An Italian boyfriend would be nice.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve written a lot about You Can See Everything, the hit documentary about Elizabeth Holmes that surprised everyone on the 2026 movie schedule. I’ve even written about a few spoilers, but now that the movie is available to buy on streaming, I’m here to ask you what the directors, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, asked us all to do months ago: keep the secrets secret! I admit it’s a little hypocritical to say that now, as I’ve spoiled the big secret in previous articles, but if you’re watching the movie with friends or loved ones on this Thanksgiving weekend and they don’t know about the spoilers, listen to the directors!

Right before the A24 film was released in September, Fielder and Oppenheim showed the movie at the New York Film Festival, and in a Q&A after the movie, Fielder talked about how the movie came to be. He mentioned that they didn’t really know where it was going to take them, or how it would end. They especially didn’t foresee the second half of the movie, and in a way, it was as much of a surprise to them as it is to audiences.

I was spoiled on the movie that seemingly everyone is talking about, from former employees of Holmes to psychologists who've seen it, before I saw it, but the two people I saw it with were not, and honestly, it was so much fun to see and hear their reactions. Fielder wants that for everyone, and he made a plea to those in attendance at the screening to keep the movie’s secrets, as hard as it might be in this social media age. Fielder said to the audience:.

The experience you guys had of, like, discovering it happening as it's happening, like we did. We really want audiences to have that experience when it opens, if possible, if you guys can preserve that in a way. I know some of you are probably going to be writing about this or whatever, but if we can preserve where we go in that section. I just love that everyone is having the experience you guys did.

Of course, it’s been a few months since the film was released and became one of the biggest box office hits of the year (and hit new milestones for documentaries), so many have either seen it or have had the massive reveal spoiled, but I do think the reveal is critical to the message of the movie.

This won’t be the last time I write about this movie, as we still have the streaming release where it'll be available with an HBO Max subscription, likely sometime in January, and You Can See Everything will undoubtedly be up for a plethora of awards over the winter. So I’ll be busy writing about it, and honestly, likely talking about the reveal, but I promise I’ll always do so with a bold spoiler warning, just as I did when the movie first came out. We should all do the same!

In a recent development, iPhone Handoff is a fresh feature in iOS 27 that lets you use the same phone number across two different iPhones. However, the feature requires carrier support, so it isn’t available to everyone. Here are the carriers that at the moment support iPhone Handoff and those that have promised support.

Sources indicate that 9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

With iPhone Handoff, you can use the same phone number on two different iPhones. Your number automatically moves between the two phones, depending on which one you pick up. This includes calls, voicemail, messages, and Find My location.

Simply unlock whichever device you want to use and you’re ready to go. Other data synced with iCloud will automatically upgrade across your devices. Third-party apps work across both devices, following each app’s own syncing behavior.

iPhone Handoff is available on iOS 27 and later. The phones must be connected to Wi-Fi, share the same Apple Account, use Messages in iCloud, and be signed into FaceTime and iMessage with the same Apple Account.

Industry observers note that the biggest limiting factor of iPhone Handoff is that it requires carrier support. At the moment, just three carriers support the feature:.

According to recent reports, what about carriers that are working on the feature? In the United States, Verizon has promised it “will support iPhone Handoff,” but it’s unclear when the feature will launch. Verizon claims it will charge $10 per month for the service.

In a recent development, AT&T, meanwhile, has no prepares to support iPhone Handoff. In a statement in September, the carrier said that its focus “remains on delivering innovations that make life simpler and keep customers connected with confidence.” The carrier noted that there “could be potential in capabilities like iPhone Handoff,” but that customers should use “existing eSIM activation and transfer options” instead.

No other carriers have promised support for iPhone Handoff, so it’s unclear how rapidly the feature will expand around the world.

In a recent development, in my testing, iPhone Handoff works really well. I have it set up between my iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. I use the iPhone Duo 90% of the time, but when I do pick up my iPhone 18 Pro, my number instantly switches to it. There’s a cute animation that expands from the Dynamic Island, confirming that the number has moved.

Landman Star Michelle Randolph's Christmas Movie Is Prime Video's Biggest Streaming Hit

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that prime Video has been serving up a feast for romantic comedy fans in 2026.
  • In a recent development, the film is called "Clashing Through the Snow" and before you immediately close this window just let me explain.
  • Recent findings suggest that until recently, Nicolas Cage and Christian Bale's sports movie "Madden" was topping the Prime Video charts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that prime Video has been serving up a feast for romantic comedy fans in 2026. Lili Reinhart's rom-com "The Love Hypothesis" just finished dominating the Prime Video charts, which came in the wake of Ester Expósito's romantic thriller "Drawn Together" becoming a Prime streaming hit. Now, the streamer has added a Christmas-themed romance just in time for the holidays, and this one stars "Landman" actor Michelle Randolph.

In a recent development, the film is called "Clashing Through the Snow" and before you immediately close this window just let me explain. Yes, the name sounds like the result of a "give me a cheesy Christmas rom-com title" ChatGPT prompt, but Randolph alone should pique your interest. The actor has quietly been delivering standout performances in Taylor Sheridan's "Landman" and his "Yellowstone" prequel "1923." The former sees her play Ainsley Norris, the ditzy but determined daughter of Billy Bob Thornton's oil man Tommy Norris. Based on her performances in those indicates, Randolph surely has a bright future ahead. While "Clashing Through the Snow" might not be her major breakthrough, it's doing pretty darn well on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that until recently, Nicolas Cage and Christian Bale's sports movie "Madden" was topping the Prime Video charts. But it's now been knocked out of the top spot by this festive romance movie, in which publishing editor Hannah Hendricks (Randolph) is forced to take a road trip with her rival, Ryan Mitchell (Chris Briney). You can see where this is going.

Recent findings suggest that according to streaming viewership tracker FlixPatrol, the film has now hit number two on the United States overall Prime Video chart (which combines TV and films) as of Thanksgiving day, and sits at number one on the movie chart. But Michelle Randolph's comedy is proving popular elsewhere, too. In fact, it's become a global hit. At the time of writing, the film is charting on 61 countries' top 10 movie rankings, which is a pretty good showing. Even more impressive, "Clashing Through the Snow" is number one on the movie charts in 47 of those countries, including the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

Meanwhile, the movie has managed to break into the overall chart in 30 countries, taking the top spot in five of them. That means "Clashing Through the Snow" is the most-watched piece of media on Prime Video in Austria, Poland, Portugal, South Africa, and Switzerland. It even managed to hit number one on the overall chart in the U.S. on November 25, 2026. That's a notable achievement, as often films will break into the top 10 movies without making it onto the overall charts. "Clashing Through the Snow" must be good, then...

"Clashing Through the Snow" is a comfortingly familiar rom-com outing that's perfect for the holidays. The film sees Chris Briney's Ryan Mitchell and Michelle Randolph's Hannah Hendricks stranded at an airport during a snowstorm, after which they share a rental car and set out on a cross-country trip to New York. The pair both need to close a deal in order to save their jobs — but wouldn't you know it, they fall in love instead. Along the way there's plenty of romantic Christmas movie moments as the couple stop in charming small towns and overcome mishaps together. Is "Clashing Through the Snow" pushing the boundaries of rom-coms? No. Is it charming? Sure is.

The film is directed by Carlson Young, who made her feature directorial debut with the 2021 fantasy horror "The Blazing World" before directing Sophie Turner in 2025's "Trust." She also oversaw a couple of Prime Video rom-coms before "Clashing Through the Snow," directing 2024's "Upgraded" and 2026's "The Last Sunrise.".

Sources indicate that now, she's delivered a major hit with her Randolph-led Christmas rom-com, which has a 77% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. There aren't enough reviews to earn it a critic score yet, but while William Bibbiani of TheWrap found it to be "unapologetically clichéd" he also found the dialogue to be memorable and saw the film as "an efficient delivery mechanism for semi-believable rom and semi-funny com.".

If that sounds appealing, "Clashing Through the Snow" is streaming on Prime Video right now.

21 Best Thanksgiving Movies to Stream This Week

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that sandwiched between the kitschy horrors of Halloween and the commercialized merriment of Christmas, Thanksgiving is often unfairly overlooked as a cinematic main course.
  • Sources indicate that nevertheless, we’ve collected 21 Thanksgiving movies (and Thanksgiving-adjacent movies) that capture the spirit of the holiday—turkey-trotting, tossing the pigskin, carb-loading, fighting with your family, and then overheating in a gorgeous cashmere sweater.
  • This isn’t known as the quintessential Thanksgiving movie for nothing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sandwiched between the kitschy horrors of Halloween and the commercialized merriment of Christmas, Thanksgiving is often unfairly overlooked as a cinematic main course. But while there might not be a feast’s worth of Thanksgiving movies, there is undoubtedly an appetite for Thanksgiving fare in film. Look no further than the inclusion of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in Miracle on 34th Street or Wednesday Adams’s sinister (if historically-accurate) re-enactment in Addams Family Values for proof that audiences love turkey’s least favorite holiday. Of course, Thanksgiving tends to get a better treatment on TV, inspiring canonical episodes of Gossip Girl, Friends, Master of None, and, of course, A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, we’ve collected 21 Thanksgiving movies (and Thanksgiving-adjacent movies) that capture the spirit of the holiday—turkey-trotting, tossing the pigskin, carb-loading, fighting with your family, and then overheating in a gorgeous cashmere sweater. Here’s to finding post-meal common ground with one of the titles on this list.

This isn’t known as the quintessential Thanksgiving movie for nothing. You know the story: Steve Martin’s uptight marketing executive, Neal, just wants to travel from Latest York to Chicago for turkey with his family. His looks for an uneventful trip are foiled again and again by John Candy’s boisterous shower-ring salesman, Del, who’s eager to make friends with Neal during their wayward journey. We will never look at pillows—or rental car agents—the same way again.

Industry observers note that don’t let the word Christmas in the title scare you away. This 2016 ensemble comedy starring Danny Glover, Kimberly Elise, Mo’Nique, and Gabrielle Union has undeniable Thanksgiving vibes. Produced by Will Packer and originally sold to Universal Pictures under the title A Meyers Thanksgiving, Almost Christmas follows the dysfunctional Meyers family as the family patriarch, Walter Meyers (Glover), tries to get through his first holiday season after the death of his wife. While it isn’t exactly about Thanksgiving per se, most of the best moments in Almost Christmas—including Elise chasing Romany Malco away from the table with a shotgun, or the whole table having to pretend to like Mo’Nique’s terrible food—take place during large family gatherings around the dinner table. What could be more Thanksgiving-coded than that? With an all-star cast of Black actors that also includes J.B. Smoove, Nicole Ari Parker, Omar Epps, and Gladys Knight, Almost Christmas feels like a homecoming full of your favorite uncles and aunties. And, to be fair, isn’t Thanksgiving almost Christmas?

The turkey isn’t the only thing getting carved up in this holiday slasher. Starring Patrick Dempsey and Tik Toker turned recording artist turned film actress Addison Rae, Thanksgiving begins with a Black Friday sale gone horribly awry in Plymouth, Massachusetts, leading to the death of multiple customers. The following year, a murderous slasher wearing a John Carver mask is wreaking havoc in Plymouth, and targeting Rae’s Gaby and her friends. If you’re not feeling warm and gooey on over the holiday, you might want to throw on Thanksgiving and watch Rae and Dempsey’s Sheriff Eric Newton try and track down and escape the clutches of a grisly murderer.

Industry observers note that in Jodie Foster’s comedy, Holly Hunter plays Claudia Larson, who returns home for Thanksgiving after losing her job and learning that her daughter (My So-Called Life–era Claire Danes) intends to spend the holiday with a boyfriend. The family she returns to is filled with colorful performances from Anne Bancroft and Charles Durning as her eclectic parents, Robert Downey Jr. as her misanthrope brother, and Dylan McDermott as a semi-mysterious dinner guest.

According to recent reports, fantastic Mr. Fox isn’t technically about Thanksgiving, or even really about humans. And yet, Wes Anderson’s 2009 stop-motion film, featuring the voices of George Clooney and Meryl Streep, has been labeled a Thanksgiving must-watch. Perhaps that’s because the film, based on Roald Dahl’s classic children’s novel, is all about animals trying to escape the tyranny of farmers—something every turkey not lucky enough to be pardoned by the president wishes it could do around Thanksgiving time. Beyond the war between animals and farmers, Anderson’s rustic color palette filled with burnt orange—and the massive feast that brings a diverse array of animals around a dinner table after they successfully joined forces to steal food from their nemeses—are full of the spirit of Thanksgiving.

According to recent reports, at times, the titular April’s (Katie Holmes) fate feels as if it rests on whether she’ll successfully cook a turkey in her crowded Lower East Side apartment. As April prepares to host her suburban Pennsylvania family, the high-stakes nature of spending a day hunkered down with relatives—played by Patricia Clarkson, Oliver Platt, Alison Pill, and John Gallagher Jr.—rushes in.

According to recent reports, sometimes getting families together over the holidays is fraught. In this 1997 moody drama directed by Ang Lee, two affluent Connecticut families unravel over Thanksgiving break as their secrets come to lights. The ensemble cast includes stalwart actors Kevin Kline, Joan Allen, Sigourney Weaver as messy parents, and, at that point, up and comers, Tobey Maguire, Elijah Wood, and Christina Ricci as their even more troubled teens. The Ice Storm, which won best screenplay at Cannes Film Festival, is rife with adultery, substance abuse, as well as surprising turns from a host of talented actors and a sharp early film from one of cinema’s most celebrated directors.

In a recent development, nothing feels more nostalgic during Thanksgiving than watching Snoopy whip up a makeshift meal with jelly beans, popcorn, and mountains of buttered toast for all of his Peanuts pals. And Vince Guraldi’s timeless score makes for a perfect soundtrack to your own festivities.

According to recent reports, A Thanksgiving flashback provides key context for the complicated dynamics amongst this group of recently-reunited college friends, played by Glenn Close, Kevin Kline, Jeff Goldblum, Mary Kay Place, and William Hurt. Lawrence Kasdan’s film earned three Oscar nominations, including best picture, original screenplay, and supporting actress for Close.

While not a Thanksgiving-themed film, protagonist Nola Darling (Tracy Camilla Johns) invites all three of her potential suitors to a tense dinner on that very holiday, making her memorable decision between them from her head-of-the-table vantage point. This was most of the world’s introduction to Spike Lee, both as an actor and director, and the electricity is still palpable. And if you’ve gotta have more? You can always stream the 2017 Netflix original series of the same name, starring Lee and DeWanda Wise as Nola Darling.

Sources indicate that rian Johnson’s whodunnit has all the trappings of a Thanksgiving movie, without ever mentioning the holiday. There’s family infighting, Chris Evans in a cable-knit sweater, foggy fall weather, and even a political allegory about the treatment of people of color. Also not about Thanksgiving, but worthy viewing for the full family: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery, which hit theaters last November.

The same year that Merriam-Webster acknowledged Instagram captions everywhere by adding “Friendsgiving” to the dictionary, a movie of the same name was released. True to its titular tradition, a group of friends convenes for a meal that inevitably devolves into chaos.

According to recent reports, while not an outright Thanksgiving movie, 1997’s ensemble dramedy contains some of the most sumptuous shots of food ever committed to film. After the death of their family matriarch, a group of disparate relatives must put aside their differences and reconvene for a weekly Sunday dinner. Starring Vivica A. Fox, Vanessa Williams, and Nia Long, Soul Food captures the bonding powers that plates of cornbread, catfish, and collard greens can bring.

This 1976 best picture Oscar winner stars Sylvester Stallone as the eponymous down-on-his-luck boxer, whose fate begins to change with the meeting of his future wife, Adrian (Talia Shire). “To you, it’s Thanksgiving. To me, it’s Thursday,” Rocky tells Adrian as he whisks her away from a disastrous family feast minutes after her brother Paulie (Burt Young) hurls her turkey into the nearby alley. As fans of the franchise, which has debuted several films over the Thanksgiving holiday, know, their Thanksgiving meet-cute will stand the test of time.

In a recent development, thanksgiving isn’t always about bickering with your blood relatives. Spend Thanksgiving with Instant Family, which stars Mark Wahlberg and Rose Byrne as Pete and Ellie Wagner, an unwitting couple who, overnight, become parents to three foster children. Their decision to become parents happens over  a tense Thanksgiving dinner where Ellie’s family shares they don’t think that Pete and Ellie were ever really cut out to be parents. In an effort to prove them wrong, the Wagners wind up biting off more than they bargained for as they become foster parents to three children, the eldest played by Madame Web star Isabela Merced.

Before Greta Gerwig forced Noah Baumbach to write Barbie with her, there was Mistress America. Written by the real-life couple who helmed the billion dollar blockbuster, this 2015 Sundance favorite centers on the unlikely friendship between Lola Kirke’s Tracy, a first-year college student alone in New York, and Gerwig’s Brooke, the Times Square-living twentysomething who will soon become her stepsister. Conflict between the pair gets resolved on Thanksgiving at New York City’s Veselka, a Ukrainian institution where pierogis stand in for the traditional bird.

Sources indicate that greta Gerwig must really love Thanksgiving. The auteur’s Oscar-nominated take on the Louisa May Alcott classic is brimming with cozy, Thanksgiving-esque vibes. Set largely in the weeks before Christmas, the March sisters (Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson, Eliza Scanlen, and Florence Pugh) and matriarch (Laura Dern) battle wits, trot through the snow, and stage living room plays in a film that feels reminiscent of many a-family gatherings.

Industry observers note that “First, let’s give thanks to our families not being here. It’s always easier without the family,” Adam Sandler’s George Simmons, a stand-up comedian who has been newly diagnosed with cancer, says to a group of fresh friends. In Judd Apatow’s 2009 dramedy, George attempts to revamp his fledgling career in the eleventh hour with the help of aspiring comic Ira Wright (Seth Rogen). At one point, he  joins the younger talent’s friendsgiving festivities, where the table is surrounded by stars including Jonah Hill, Jason Schwartzman, Aubrey Plaza, and Bo Burnham.

In a recent development, in one of the newer entries to the turkey day canon, Stephen Karam adapts his 2015 Pulitzer finalist play of the same name, exploring the long-held resentments and deeply-rooted admiration that live in an East Coast family. Jayne Houdyshell reprises her Tony-winning role as Deirdre alongside a stacked ensemble, including Richard Jenkins, June Squibb, Beanie Feldstein, Steven Yeun, and Amy Schumer, all gathered in a drab Chinatown apartment for Thanksgiving.

Prisoners finds Hugh Jackman and Jake Gyllenhaal teaming up to find a pair of missing girls who were abducted after Thanksgiving dinner in Conyers, Pennsylvania. EGOT recipient Viola Davis also stars in the thriller as the mother of one of the kidnapped girls. Directed by Dune’s Denis Villeneuve, Prisoners is an unconventional and unsettling Thanksgiving film.

In a recent development, another unconventional choice, Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man is arguably the only superhero movie that doubles as a Thanksgiving movie. While the central action follows Tobey Maguire’s Peter Parker, there’s a pivotal scene set at Thanksgiving dinner that directly follows a heated battle between Spider-Man and the Green Goblin (a.k.a Norman Osborne, played by Willem Dafoe.) Parker and Osborne have Thanksgiving dinner together with MJ (Kirsten Dunst), Harry Osborne (James Franco), and Aunt May (Rosemary Harris). During the meal, Osborne comes to the stunning realization that Peter Parker is, in fact, Spider-Man. Others have already made the case that the first Spider-Man film deserves to be included in the Thanksgiving canon. The way Dafoe carves the turkey is also both sinister and iconic, as is Maguire apologizing for his tardiness because he “had to beat an old lady with a stick to get these cranberries.”.

The debate over the wisdom and safety of using Meta’s Muse AI agent continues as the app rolls out in the UK. It follows a warning by a number of regulatory bodies about the potential risks of AI agents ….

Meta yesterday announced the UK availability of Muse.

Industry observers note that muse, Meta’s personal Al agent, is now available to adults in the UK. Think of it as a helping hand for the jobs that pile up, like chasing a refund, renewing car insurance or keeping on top of the school calendar. A forum representing four different UK regulatory bodies last month issued a warning about the potential dangers involved in using AI agents. The Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum said:.

AI agents may amplify and accelerate risks and introduce newly introduced ones. These risks may increase as the capabilities of personal agents grow and adoption rises. Questions of consumer protection, competition and data protection – for example the risk of fraud and scams, personal information sharing not in line with user expectations and misleading recommendations, decisions or information provided – must be addressed to ensure innovation develops in ways that earn and maintain public trust.

It has been revealed that meta has pushed back against suggestions that Muse has accessed personal data without permission, insisting that users are in control and must approve key actions. The organization has admitted to some “isolated incidents,” but claims other reported breaches were either hallucinations or took place on internal versions of the app while undergoing testing. In a newly introduced blog post, Meta says:.

Sources indicate that muse only works with the apps and services you choose to connect it to, and you control the access it gets […] Once you’ve decided what Muse is connected to and what you want it to do, with your oversight, it can handle tasks like searching, comparing and planning for you. But before it does anything like sending an email or buying something, it shows you exactly what it’s about to do and waits for your go-ahead. A separate security agent checks Muse’s actions and the information it sends out against the permissions you’ve granted. You can also choose how often it checks in with you in Settings.

At the time of writing, Muse remains the second most popular free app in Apple’s US App Store, with more than 10 million downloads. Brainwashing Easter egg walkthrough in GTA 6

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1712 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the brainwashing Easter egg in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a long side mission in which you get the chance to investigate long-forgotten bunkers where a certain president spent some time (and listened to rumba) and where brainwashing experiments had taken place.
  • To help you uncover the mystery regarding President Russo, here's how to start the 'Kill The President' Easter egg in GTA 6 and how to complete it.
  • According to recent reports, to start the "Kill the President" quest chain, you must talk to José Bermúdez, a man sitting in front of the Joe Russo monument in Downtown, Vice City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the brainwashing Easter egg in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a long side mission in which you get the chance to investigate long-forgotten bunkers where a certain president spent some time (and listened to rumba) and where brainwashing experiments had taken place. Like the Vice City portal Easter egg, you'll need to go through a series of steps to finish this mission, but there's no other option if you want to learn the truth about what the government hid from you.

To help you uncover the mystery regarding President Russo, here's how to start the 'Kill The President' Easter egg in GTA 6 and how to complete it.

According to recent reports, to start the "Kill the President" quest chain, you must talk to José Bermúdez, a man sitting in front of the Joe Russo monument in Downtown, Vice City. Be sure to visit him during the day! Choose to ask "What really happened?" after he starts talking. José will tell you to visit his apartment in a salmon-colored building with Cuban flags on Little Cuba NW 4th avenue if you want to know the truth.

Sources indicate that go to his place to find the blueprint of a bunker on the wall, some recordings, and a picture showing President Russo on Sharktooth Island — your next destination. Before you go, be sure to listen to the recording and pay attention to what President Russo claims, as he'll tell you the code for the next area.

Recent findings suggest that travel northeast on the map to find Sharktooth Island, on the southern side of Little Hardin Island in Leonard County. Once you reach the island, head northwest to find the bunker entrance and a keypad lock that requires a six-digit number.

According to recent reports, unfortunately, you won't find the code on the island. The information you need to figure out the code was shared by President Russo himself in the recording you found in José's apartment. Now, if you don't want to return to the apartment just to listen to the recording again, don't worry. The code to open the bunker is 010317.

In a recent development, as you enter the bunk, turn right to find an electrical box. Pull the lever up to turn the lights on, then head in the opposite direction. After passing through a couple of small rooms, you will get to a larger room where you'll find some beds and a presidential desk beside a large safe.

Sources indicate that sit in the chair behind the desk and look to your right for the "Search drawer" option to appear. Next, pick up the phone. Inside the drawer, you will find a file with three different number sequences listed below the word "Protocol." Keep these in mind.

The next step is to return to one of the first rooms you passed through and listen to the recordings, in which someone mentions the number "5297" and "protocol two." These are the clues you need to open the safe.

If you want a quick answer to how to open the safe in the presidential bunker, you need to move the last number to the front to get the safe code, which is 2975. Inside, you will find Russo's 1922 pistol and a photo. It appears to show part of the map with arrows pointing to a specific location. If you flip it, you can read the word "OBSESS" on the back of the photo. Now, it's time to locate the place in the photo.

Sources indicate that the photo you found inside the safe in the presidential bunker shows the location of another bunker in Grassrivers, Mariana County. You can reach it by heading southwest from the Richardson Hunting Supplies shop, but you can't enter through the main entrance. Instead, you will need to open the hatch, which you find to the northeast.

As expected of a secret bunker, the hatch is locked, and you will need to enter a six-digit number to open it. Luckily, you've opened the safe in the presidential bunker and seen the word behind the photo. Don't you think some letters look like numbers? If you make the numbers out, you'll get 085355.

Industry observers note that once you're inside the bunker, there isn't much to do besides make your way through the rooms on the left side to reach the electrical box and turn on the lights. Next, return to the starting portion of the area and follow the path through the rooms on the right side until you reach a half-open metal door leading to a control room.

Press the two red buttons on the main panel. The lights on the garage will turn on, and the door to your right will open. You can now enter the garage, where you will find a tank, the Cold War 556 unique assault rifle, some ammo and grenades. From this point on, the main entrance will remain open, so you can use it if you return here whenever you'd like.

Enjoy the rewards, but this quest is far from over. Return to the main area of the bunker and look for the first room on the right side, where there's a chair and a TV that's now turned on.

Industry observers note that sit on the chair, and you will be transported to the past and the game's perspective changes to a first-person view. While in this dimension, you will be trapped in a loop that only allows you to move forward through the corridor. To return to a previous room, you will need to circle all the way back.

The first step is to leave the room and follow the main corridor until you loop back to where you started. Enter the room where you woke up and answer the phone. The voice on the other end will mention that patients have become obsessed with time and that maybe they should get rid of the clock.

Following this clue will lead to the reception area, the only place where you'll find a clock. On the right side of the room, there's a locked door that requires a six-digit number to open. Ignore it for now, because you don't have enough information to discover the code yet. Interact with the clock to time travel to the future, where you'll find a run-down version of the institute. Take another walk around until you reach the corridor before the reception area. A telephone will ring. Jump through the broken window to enter the room and answer the phone. Pay attention to what the scientist says about the three candidates.

Sources indicate that take another lap until you reach the corridor with the candidates' room, where there are multiple beds. Use your focus to reveal the traces showing where three candidates have gone. Now, if you remember what you heard in the last phone call, the scientist mentioned three people in a specific order. To identify them, you must remember what each person did, so you can trace them back to their respective beds. Once you've figured that out, go back to the past using the clock to see the numbers on the wall. Put the password together by using the numbers in the correct order.

If you don't want to spend time playing detective and analyzing the paths in the candidates' room, here's the code: 090607.

Industry observers note that with the password in hand, return to the past and open the room on the right side of the reception area. Inside, you will find a control room with a red telephone and a computer. To access the computer, you will need to form a password using the options displayed in the bottom-right corner of the screen. Although it is possible to find the answer through trial and error, there's one way to discover the password: answer the call.

After you pick up the telephone, the scientist will once again share information about the program and the candidates, including clues you need to figure out the computer password. He mentions something about the target, the date, and the fact that the candidates are losing their sense of time.

According to recent reports, although there are no meditation spots in this dimension for Lucia or Jason to look at within themselves, they can metaphorically achieve this by looking at their picture hung in the lab. Press L2 on PS5 or LT on Xbox Series X, then hold R2 or RT until the area around the screen turns red. Then, look down to see that a little box open, revealing a Duke 1922 pistol. Take it and your training will be completed.

In a recent development, return to the past by interacting with the clock, head to the computer that you used earlier. This time, select the "Break the Cycle" option. It will open the exterior containment door, also known as the red door, in the reception area. President Russo had been standing in front of it since you started walking around these corridors. However, this time he won't be there. Open the door and enjoy.

After completing the mission, you will return to reality, unlock the "Brainwashed" award tattoo design and find the Brainwasher 1922 unique pistol beside the TV.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if there’s one major day to circle on what’s left of the 2026 movie schedule, it’s Dunesday. It’s the Friday before Christmas when both Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three are hitting theaters. It’s going to be a huge weekend for the movie business regardless, but the writer and director of Dune 3, Denis Villeneuve, just shared his thoughts on it, and he’s not happy. However, does he have the right to be? Let’s break it down.

First, what exactly did the Dune filmmaker say about Dunesday? In a fresh interview with Time, the director, who’s completing the trilogy with Part Three, didn’t hold back, saying this:.

Sources indicate that listen, I will be honest. The first Dune came out at the end of the pandemic. We made a great box office in a very rough environment. But we had the winds against us. Then the second movie, same thing. We were meant to release in the fall, and we had to release at the end of winter because of the two Hollywood strikes. We had success, but it was not easy. The third time, I stated to myself, 'Finally, there is no pandemic, no strike in sight. We will have a normal release.' Then Disney put the biggest franchise of all time against us. I’m no fool. Those movies are a mammoth.

Sources indicate that as he points to, the first Dune came out in October 2021 at a time when theaters were still struggling in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite this, the movie made $410.7 million worldwide against a budget of $165 million. Then, the 2024 sequel did even better with a $714.9 million global haul, but that was after it had to be pushed back due to the 2023 Hollywood strikes.

Industry observers note that going into Dune 3, Villeneuve thought the franchise’s struggles would be over, but then Avengers: Doomsday moved its release date to open next to it. The director also noted this:.

Sources indicate that so I was deeply disappointed. But we had committed to this date, to IMAX. It was impossible to move. So I accepted my fate, praying to the gods of cinema. Dune is not a mammoth like the Avengers, but it’s a sexy little animal that has a lot of firepower, and I hope we will survive. It could be one of the biggest box-office weekends of all time because of both movies. Am I in competition with the Avengers? Absolutely not. It’s a T. rex. But I stand proud because I think the film delivers.

In a recent development, while the paired billing of Barbie and Oppenheimer back in 2023 famously helped both films become meteoric successes at the box office, Villeneuve doesn’t have that point of view for Dunesday. The Avengers films have been known to break huge records, and sharing the date with the latest of them has left him “praying to the gods of cinema” for his own epic.

Sources indicate that so, what do the latest numbers say about Dunesday with December 18 just three weeks away? According to the most current projection of $270 million, Avengers: Doomsday already has the highest box office projection the National Research Group has ever recorded (via Deadline). Yes, even higher than Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which recently broke Endgame’s domestic opening weekend record over the summer.

In a recent development, dune: Part 3, on the other hand, is tracking at around $75 million, with projections suggesting it “wouldn’t be shocking” if it passes $80 million. That would be on par with the previous Dune movie and double the debut earnings of the first film. Plus, as Villeneuve noted, Dune: Part 3 could contribute to one of the biggest box office openings of all time.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In a recent development, so, clearly Dune is not topping Avengers: Doomsday. The major con here is Doomsday is definitely robbing the final Dune film of a No. 1 slot at the box office. However, as the director said, he’s not expecting Avengers numbers for his own film. The other thing to keep in mind is some fans of both franchises might pick Doomsday over Dune. But, let's be real here, I'd assume most fans of both are going to see both in theaters opening weekend some way, somehow! We'll have to wait and see if Doomsday boosts Dune sales, but either way, both movies aren't expected to flop; Doomsday is just a behemoth of a movie impossible to compete against.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

John Hughes made some of the most beloved movies of all time in his eight directorial efforts, to the point where it's nearly impossible to rank the films he wrote and directed. Still, there are few movies that reach the specific balance of comedy with such an emotional punch as Hughes does in 1987's "Planes, Trains and Automobiles." This is a goofball movie that borders on the surreal, with some of the most bizarre imagery in a comedy movie, while also delivering some of the most heartbreaking and heartwarming moments that came out of the 1980s.

The film stars Steve Martin as Neal Page, an uptight marketing executive forced to be paired with Del Griffith (John Candy), a goofball salesman with a heart of gold, when their journey from New York City to Chicago is disrupted. What was meant to be just a short cab and plane ride home just in time for Thanksgiving ends up being a three-day odyssey full of shenanigans, attempted murder, and much more.

It has been revealed that it's no wonder, then, that "Planes, Trains and Automobiles" is the No. 1 movie streaming on Paramount+ on Thanksgiving Day 2026. After all, there are plenty of movies about Christmas, to the point where it's easy to overlook Thanksgiving, and with good reason. For one, it's not really a holiday outside the U.S. and Canada (and even then, celebrated on different days), and the imagery is not dissimilar to Christmas anyway. Still, the best Thanksgiving movies deliver a very specific tone that's less about holiday magic and more about celebrating what we have despite the horrors of daily life. From the opening minutes of "Planes, Trains and Automobiles," it's clear this movie could not be set at any other time of year except during the chaos and anxiety of Thanksgiving.

The travel chaos that is quite unique to Thanksgiving is the crux of "Planes, Trains and Automobiles." The arrival of snowstorms that plague the East Coast of the continental United States, the huge flux of travelers, and the general anxiety and irritability of travelers around the country add to, well, a very stressful time of year. It's why Steve Martin's uptight businessman Neal is so relatable. The film simply nails the feeling of needing to interact with others and ask for their help while being utterly frustrated with having to deal with anyone at such a bad time. It's also why John Candy's performance is such a tightrope, because his character has to be annoying in addition to being charming. Del's not really someone you'd want as a travel companion, yet he is absolutely the best person you want as a friend.

That tricky balance is what makes the movie so memorable, and why John Candy's best line remains the best Thanksgiving movie quote ever. Neal and Del are forced to not only set aside their differences, but actually recognize the humanity in each other while acknowledging that they themselves are flawed. This is a highly empathetic film that's all about how we should find love and camaraderie even in unlikely companions. That is why the film so perfectly captures the spirit of Thanksgiving, because it's not about estranged family members, but rather complete strangers who must come to learn they need one another and that they should be grateful for what they bring into each other's lives. Togetherness is not just for family members, or even people you like, but also for strangers you come to appreciate despite the ways they annoy you.

Recent findings suggest that kpop Demon Hunters remains one of the defining films of its era. Released last year to strong reviews and a rapturous reception by general audiences, the movie (and its soundtrack) swiftly became pop culture fixtures on a global scale. The sequel is presently in development, with worldwide musical tours set to keep love for the film thriving for years to come.

Industry observers note that the fact that the movie debuted on Netflix is part of that success, with the streaming service being a perfect place for fans to watch and rewatch the film to their heart's content. However, there's always been something about the movie that separated it from most original films that debut on the service. In fact, that sense of scale is a massive reason why it connected so well.

In a recent development, it's also why Kpop Demon Hunters makes perfect sense as a Criterion Collection release. The movie never felt right constrained to a purely online experience, with the home release highlighting the craft and care that went into the movie through a lot of exclusive additions. It's a perfect addition to the Collection and a terrific showcase for why home media still has a place in the modern movie marketplace.

Kpop Demon Hunters is the rare film that released on a streaming service that feels like it wasn't necessarily made for that kind of platform. Entering development in 2018, the film was formally added to the Sony Pictures Animation slate, with likely intentions to bring it the big screen.

Sources indicate that in 2023, the film was formally added to the Netflix film slate as part of a collaborative deal between the studio and the streamer, eventually launching on the streaming service in 2025. Unlike a lot of other films released for streaming that are criticized for their limited scope and specific scale, Kpop Demon Hunters has a larger-than-life quality that's befitting the biggest screen possible.

Sources indicate that beyond the impressive visuals and tight action, the unifying vibes that come with the film's narrative and music make it the ideal movie to watch with larger groups. That's evidenced by the massive success the film has found in its short theatrical runs, which elicited surprisingly robust box office returns.

While the film's streaming release definitely contributed to its massive success - being able to rewatch it at leisure and throw impromptu watch parties gave the film a lot more legs than it might have otherwise - the film's true strength is that it feels genuinely epic. The fights have a showy quality that hides a lot of depth, while the musical numbers and visual gags have plenty to deconstruct.

It has been revealed that the vibrancy of the animation makes it stand out from other films, coupled with the character design and sense of motion lends, it an anime-influenced tenor that feels wholly unique. It's a painfully unique film that feels deeply authentic to South Korean culture, without ever sacrificing its larger-than-life qualities for that grounding touch.

Industry observers note that more than anything, Kpop Demon Hunters avoids the kind of repetitive dialogue and basic plot beats that many streaming movies are criticized for. While there are plenty of great movies released directly for streaming, there's often a sense of contained focus to those films that reflects the streaming model and set-up.

They need to be simple enough to have on in the background, when the best movies are the ones that command attention. Kpop Demon Hunters proves that a streaming service film can still have that sense of scale to feel like an entirely different world, all while still being grounded with character and comedy.

It feels like the kind of movie that only comes about because of years of craft and a lifetime's worth of passion. Streaming is great for audiences, but it's nice to see a movie launch on a platform that feels like so much more than what audiences have come to expect from those kinds of debuts.

All of the craft that went into the film can be overlooked on streaming services, which benefit from being able to give audiences a non-stop amount of content to fall into. However, that's where the likes of the Criterion Collection come into play. The distribution company has always been dedicated to elevating movie releases, showcasing the full depth of the filmmaking process that goes into every release.

According to recent reports, the KPop Demon Hunters Criterion release is no different, with the kind of detailed additional elements that Netflix simply can't put alongside the film. The release contains a feature-length animatic for the film, highlighting its earliest complete setup. It includes a making-of documentary as well as video essays, focused on the artistic intention behind the film and the impact it has had on audiences.

It's the sort of thing home releases for films have that streaming just can't match. It's the kind of material that super fans and cinema nerds can dive into, gaining a fuller appreciation for the movie and everything going on behind the scenes. Movies like KPop Demon Hunters deserve that kind of showcase, not just because of the craft that went into it, but because of how much love the film has garnered since it came out.

Recent findings suggest that it's the kind of attention that streaming just isn't designed for. In an era where home media is increasingly being phased out in favor of digital-only platforms, stuff like the Criterion Collection highlights what home media can offer that streamers simply can't. For film aficionados and die-hard fans alike, the Criterion Collection release of KPop Demon Hunters is a perfect addition to a personal library.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how owners open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it.

Opening Notification Center is unchanged on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 by default. However, enabling Siri AI changes a key swipe gesture on both iPhone and iPad.

One of the many ways of invoking Siri AI, once enabled, is by swiping down from the center of the top edge of your iPhone or iPad display. This previously opened Notification Center.

Recent findings suggest that you can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner once Siri AI is enabled. Alerts now animate in from the top left corner. This is a way to point customers toward Notification Center’s smaller surface area.

Apple is greatly prioritizing Siri AI access in iOS 27. The majority of the top edge is devoted to invoking the new Siri experience.

In a recent development, the last time Apple made a change to accessing Notification Center came when Control Center moved from a swipe up gesture from the bottom to a top-right corner swipe down gesture on iPhone X. Apple later unified this experience across devices.

Now it’s Notification Center’s turn to be put in the corner. On iPadOS 27 beta 1 in particular, the area above Home screen app icons was pretty much devoted to invoking Siri AI. The area for opening Notification Center actually shrank if you disable displaying AM/PM or the date.

Sources indicate that I've been always swiping from the left corner to see my notifications. I didn't even know you could swipe from the center to get to it as well 😂 I guess I'm good then?

Apple improved this with iPadOS 27 beta 2, creating a more uniform region on either side. It’s roughly the size of two app columns with Notification Center on the left and Control Center on the right. The rest is for invoking Siri.

After 15 years of muscle memory, it’ll take some time to determine if this change is worth it or something that should be reconsidered. In the meantime, early feedback sounds overwhelmingly positive around Apple’s newly introduced Siri AI system. Hearing that Siri is good now will also take some getting used to, I’m sure.

After months of using the new behavior, I’m certain I’d toggle it off if there were a setting to do so. Since there’s no option to disable invoking Siri from the top middle swipe down, the only thing to do is build new muscle memory around avoiding the center.

What do you think? Would you change this back if you could? Is accessing Siri from the swipe-down gesture worth the change? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Ingrid Bergman and Roberto Rossellini: The Affair That Outraged America

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
